[](https://substack.com/redirect/542709ad-fdda-46ca-85ba-3e9774d97755?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### Ahmed Abu Al-Kas and others remove debris and body parts after a strike on a residential tower in Gaza City on August 2, 2026. Video by Mohamed Ahmed.
The surge in Israeli attacks came in the wake of a deal with Hamas, first announced by Trump on Thursday, on a roadmap for implementing the next phases of the Gaza "ceasefire." Shortly after Trump's announcement, mediator countries said Hamas had, "for the first time," formally committed to "an actionable plan for relinquishing all its weapons."
The following day, Hamas said it had engaged "responsibly and positively" with mediators' proposals but stressed that implementation of the deal would only proceed if Israel fulfilled all of its obligations under the first phase of the October 2025 agreement. The group said discussions over handing over its heavy weapons were conditional on a permanent end to Israeli attacks, a full Israeli withdrawal from Gaza, early recovery and reconstruction, the entry of a Palestinian technocratic committee and international forces, the dismantling of Israel-backed armed militias, and progress toward Palestinian self-determination and an independent Palestinian state.
While Tel Aviv did not initially issue a formal response, Israeli officials were quickly quoted in the press saying they rejected the deal as the escalated weekend assault began.
On Saturday, at least six Palestinians were killed in a series of airstrikes, including one targeting the area of Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al Balah, damaging an adjacent medical storage facility and destroying essential medical supplies as well as a number of tents sheltering displaced families.
"We went to sleep under a [new ceasefire deal]. Trump announced a ceasefire and things were going in the right direction....We slept peacefully and happily, thinking that the situation would get better from the next day onward," Fatima Sharab, who was displaced from her home and living in a tent near Al-Aqsa Hospital, told Drop Site. She said she was woken up at around 2 a.m. on Saturday morning with instructions to flee the area before it was bombed.
Sharab stood among shredded tents and belongings that littered the ground next to a massive crater in the sand. "The camp here is made up of tents and a warehouse for kidney medications for dialysis patients. So what was the problem? What did we do wrong?" She added, "You can't even tell where your own tent was or where your belongings are. Today, we have no shelter. I don't even know what to say anymore."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/50375be5-9dcf-4787-aedb-cd0a47b36db8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### The aftermath of an Israeli strike near Al-Aqsa Hospital in Deir al-Balah on August 1, 2026. Video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
According to the director of Al-Aqsa Hospital, Raed Hussein, the warehouse that was targeted on Saturday was the main one of four the hospital established in coordination with the World Health Organization to help deal with a storage crisis. "This warehouse contained all the solutions and equipment needed for kidney dialysis," Hussein told Drop Site. "We were shocked to wake up today and find that this warehouse had been targeted...Over the past three years, supplies have never been fully available, and when they do arrive, they come only in limited quantities. So you can imagine the consequences of this attack."
The heavy assault continued the next day when an Israeli missile slammed into Al-Thawra street in western Gaza City, killing a child and a bridegroom [in his tent](https://substack.com/redirect/2cf2cb84-f25c-45d1-bcab-04e76d95fe2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
"He was preparing his tent for his wedding, then he was torn apart in it," said Rasem Asaliya, 35, an eyewitness. "They said there would be a ceasefire, no more strikes, no more assassinations. But they struck anyway."
The torn, blood-spattered tent barely stood upright next to a small crater where the missile struck. "They are still attacking us and our children. Nothing has changed. They're liars. They broke their word," said Mohamed Yassin, 37, who rushed to the site in the aftermath of the attack. "All the news we're hearing [about a new deal] is a lie. This isn't news; it's all false propaganda."
On Monday, three countries that have served as mediators--Qatar, Egypt, and Turkey--issued their first joint statement condemning the Israeli attacks. They denounced Israel's targeting of healthcare facilities and medical infrastructure, and the killing of civilians, including women and children, calling the attacks "a flagrant violation of international law and international humanitarian law."
At the same time, Nickolay Mladenov, the High Representative of Board of Peace, along with other board members, met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The board issued a statement shortly afterwards saying "Israel and the Board of Peace share a common understanding of the ultimate objectives." The statement clarified a series of measures that contravened the board's own roadmap, saying Hamas must first fully disarm before Israel took any steps. "Contrary to inaccurate reports, we note that the withdrawal of the IDF [Israel Defense Forces] beyond the Yellow Line will take place only once decommissioning is complete, as Hamas committed to the mediators. This applies to light weapons, heavy weapons, and the tunnels alike," the board said.
In his first public comments on the agreement on Tuesday, Netanyahu flatly rejected the deal. "They sent us a draft. We did not agree. It is not our draft. We sent our comments," he said in a video posted on social media. "We're not withdrawing from our current lines until Hamas is totally disarmed."
Since the "ceasefire" agreement went into effect nearly 10 months ago, Israel has violated the terms of the deal on a daily basis. Over 1,250 Palestinians have been killed, including over 300 children, in routine airstrikes, shelling, and shooting. Israel has not allowed in the agreed upon levels of humanitarian aid and life essentials, blocked the entry of reconstructions equipment and shelters, refused to fully open the Rafah border crossing, and has gradually pushed in its ground troops further westward from what was supposed to be an initial line of withdrawal of 53% of Gaza to now controlling nearly 70% of the enclave.
The pace of killing has been gradually increasing. Gaza's Health Ministry recently noted that 152 people were killed during the month of July, including 21 children, marking the highest monthly death toll recorded since the beginning of 2026 in what has been a steady escalation over the past few months.
The official death toll since the beginning of Israel's genocidal assault in October 2023 has now topped 73,300 with over 174,200 injured. Thousands more are missing and trapped under the rubble. Denied proper equipment and resources, Civil Defense crews have been unable to properly retrieve the bodies.
Over the weekend, first responders managed to complete intensive efforts to recover the remains of 112 Palestinians, including 40 children, killed in one of the deadliest single incidents of the genocide--an Israeli attack on a residential block in the Sabra neighborhood of Gaza City on November 22, 2023 that killed over 300 members of the Hassayna and Abu Sharia families in what Amnesty International called "a chilling illustration of a pattern of Israeli attacks wiping out entire multi-generational families."
A mass funeral ceremony was held on Tuesday for the 112 retrieved bodies in what was understood to be the largest funeral in Gaza's modern history. The bodies, wrapped in Palestinian flags, were carried on stretchers through the destroyed streets of Gaza City before being laid in rows on the ground for the funeral prayer. They were then brought to a nearby cemetery to be laid to rest.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/d1894b8e-7acd-426f-bb9c-f70773ef6672?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### A mass funeral ceremony in Gaza City for the remains of 112 Palestinians retrieved from under the rubble after an Israeli attack on a residential block in the Sabra neighborhood in November 2023. Video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
"This overwhelming scene reminds us of the crimes and attacks committed by the Israeli occupation, and its brutality and criminality against these families," Fares Affana, the Civil Defense Director of Ambulance and Emergency Services in North Gaza told Drop Site. "This massacre is one of the largest carried out in the Gaza Strip. We could hear the cries and screams of the wounded from beneath the rubble of such massacres. Some were wounded and still alive. But because of our lack of equipment, we couldn't reach them."
Another mourner watched as the martyrs were carried through the streets. "Those whose bodies were recovered from beneath the rubble and debris embody for the world the devotion to the Palestinian cause," he said. "This is not a funeral for one family alone. It is a funeral for all of Gaza."

name: Tim Burchett
subject: What happened behind closed doors
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Burchett for Congress
body:
Bureaucrats dodge. Insiders protect insiders. But I keep digging.

| [](https://trk.email.tim-burchett._8mDSa-BRSQKA)
---
Recently, I walked into another classified briefing.
As a Member of Congress, that is part of my job. And there are things discussed in those rooms that I simply cannot repeat.
Some information must remain classified to protect our country, our service members, and our intelligence operations.
But here is what I can tell you: [The American people deserve leaders who ask hard questions, not politicians who nod along, memorize the approved talking points, and shuffle back out the door.](https://trk.email.tim-burchett._3dl29uLSFWFR8d353Q)
Whether it is government waste, border security, taxpayer dollars winding up in the wrong hands, or information the bureaucracy would rather keep buried, Congress has a duty to demand answers.
Too often, Washington’s response boils down to: [“Don’t worry about it.”](https://trk.email.tim-burchett._Dag)
Well, I do worry about it.
I worry because I work for the people who sent me here, not the corrupt insiders, unelected bureaucrats, or sewer rats scurrying around Washington.
There are plenty of folks in this town who would be tickled pink if Members of Congress stopped asking questions, kept their mouths shut, and left the establishment alone.
I am not one of them.
I did not come to Washington to sit quietly while bureaucrats dodge questions, insiders protect one another, and taxpayers get stuck with the bill.
I came here to raise Cain, demand answers, and make the DC cartel mighty uncomfortable.
[Peter, will you chip in whatever you can swing today to help me keep after them?](https://trk.email.tim-burchett._4oQ)

| | **Goldman Says Brent Stays $80–$90 Until a Deal Is Signed. Beneath the Headlines, Physical Oil Inventories Are Drawing Down 6.3 Million Barrels a Day. Here Is What That Means for Gas Prices.**
---
| | Goldman Sachs put a precise structure on the oil market: Brent stays in an $80–$90 range until there is either confirmation of a signed US-Iran agreement or a significant escalation. This week tested both edges — the Qatar interim proposal pushed Brent below $79, the Geneva postponement lifted it back to $80–$81. **But beneath the diplomacy, the physical oil market is tightening in a way that complicates the supply-glut story.** Goldman’s global visible-stocks counter showed inventories falling by 6.3 million barrels per day over the past two weeks — driven by lower Persian Gulf and Red Sea flows, reduced Russian exports, and stronger Asian imports including from China.
---
| | This matters for your gas prices because it runs counter to the four-front supply loosening story from earlier in the week. OPEC+ restored its cuts and alternative pipelines resumed, but actual visible inventories are drawing down, not building. **The physical market is tighter than the loosening headlines suggest, which is why Brent found support at $80 rather than continuing toward $72.** For the American driver, this means the ~$0.45 per gallon of relief that looked likely midweek when Brent was below $79 is now partially on hold. At $80–$81 Brent, gasoline near $3.99 falls more slowly — perhaps $0.20–$0.25 over the coming weeks rather than the full $0.45. A signed deal would resume the decline. A continued physical draw could halt it entirely.
---

When you buy produce at the grocery store, you’re trusting an entire system working quietly behind the scenes: microbiologists tracing infections, food safety inspectors testing crops, and public health experts stopping contaminated products before they ever reach your kitchen table. You usually only hear about them when something goes wrong. **And right now, something is going terribly wrong.**

body:

# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136726587/638407358/-343666687?refcode=AU_GWN_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260805_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODMxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZjMwODcyYy05ZjkxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uc76HBLxHmV7iFHixuqpA1GsI1KvoJm9Y-J3RCwbPT4=&emci=4919b1cb-0991-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=2f30872c-9f91-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=28008880)
---
Peter, On January 1st I'll take office as your next Wake County District Attorney. The job is simple: keep our community safe, fight violent crime, stand up for victims, and prosecute public corruption. But I need to tell you about a decision made in Raleigh that's going to make that job much harder. This year's state budget funded 18 new prosecutors across North Carolina. Wake County got zero — even though we're the state's largest county and, by the court's own formula, already one of the most understaffed offices in the state. **WRAL, July 3, 2026:**
"'Playing politics with public safety': NC budget makes Wake DA office state's most understaffed" **[read the full story →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136726589/638407360/-35130537?refcode=AU_GWN_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260805_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODMxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZjMwODcyYy05ZjkxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uc76HBLxHmV7iFHixuqpA1GsI1KvoJm9Y-J3RCwbPT4=&emci=4919b1cb-0991-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=2f30872c-9f91-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=28008880)** When I take office, I'll inherit the most understaffed prosecutor's office in North Carolina, with less than 65% of the prosecutors the state's own workload formula says we need. This wasn't an accident. House Republicans funded new prosecutors in districts above us and below us, and left Wake — the largest county in the state — with zero. You don't leave out the biggest county by mistake. Legislative Republicans in the House made a choice, and Wake County is paying for it. Here's what that means in real terms. Wake County has 45 prosecutors. Mecklenburg — a smaller county — has 95. That leaves the average Wake prosecutor responsible for more than 2,600 cases a year, against just 1,080 in Mecklenburg. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136726592/638407363/703255683?refcode=AU_GWN_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260805_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODMxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZjMwODcyYy05ZjkxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uc76HBLxHmV7iFHixuqpA1GsI1KvoJm9Y-J3RCwbPT4=) No prosecutor can give every victim and every case the attention it deserves under that load. Ours work incredibly hard. They're just being asked to do too much with too little. When cases back up, victims wait years instead of months for justice, and repeat offenders stay out on our streets much longer. Justice delayed isn't just frustrating. It's a public safety problem for everyone in Wake County. And I'll be honest with you: when prosecutors are stretched this thin, things fall through the cracks. That's not a knock on the people doing the work. It's basic math — and it's the direct result of a choice made by Republicans in Raleigh. So how did this happen? Before the budget was finalized, I repeatedly asked Representative Mike Schietzelt to meet about the staffing crisis. He refused — wouldn't meet, wouldn't even take a call. Representative Erin Paré did speak with me, and I appreciate that. But when the budget became law, Wake still got zero. Representative Schietzelt later gave a floor speech celebrating the 18 new prosecutors the legislature funded statewide. He left out the fact that his own county got none of them. That leaves a simple question: if our state representatives won't fight for Wake County on something as basic as public safety, who will? Public safety shouldn't be partisan. Victims aren't Republicans or Democrats. They're our neighbors, and they deserve a justice system that works for everyone. This fight isn't over. I'll keep speaking out until Wake County gets the prosecutors our community needs. If you agree that public safety should come before politics:
* Forward this email.
* Contact Wake County's two GOP representatives, **[Mike Schietzelt](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136726594/638407365/1815246754?refcode=AU_GWN_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260805_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODMxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZjMwODcyYy05ZjkxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uc76HBLxHmV7iFHixuqpA1GsI1KvoJm9Y-J3RCwbPT4=&emci=4919b1cb-0991-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=2f30872c-9f91-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=28008880)** and **[Erin Paré](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136726596/638407367/1875354253?refcode=AU_GWN_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260805_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODMxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZjMwODcyYy05ZjkxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uc76HBLxHmV7iFHixuqpA1GsI1KvoJm9Y-J3RCwbPT4=&emci=4919b1cb-0991-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=2f30872c-9f91-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=28008880)** , and ask why Wake County got zero. Their party is in charge. It's their budget.
* Share the staffing graphic.
* Talk to your friends and neighbors.

Our families deserve a justice system that works for everyone. Together, we're going to keep fighting until Wake County gets the resources it deserves. Thank you,
Wiley Nickel | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136726598/638407369/703255683?refcode=AU_GWN_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260805_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODMxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZjMwODcyYy05ZjkxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uc76HBLxHmV7iFHixuqpA1GsI1KvoJm9Y-J3RCwbPT4=)

We started with four people, my wife and our two daughters, in a funeral home chapel. It was a place for people who were hurting or had questions or doubts. Now, the church is the largest in Kansas. Even all these years later, I’m proud to say that mission hasn't changed.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. # **Mamdani booed off stage at Staten Island NYPD event "Get the f**k outta here!"**
Mayor Zohran Mamdani was **[met with loud boos,](https://substack.com/redirect/a6c07fef-abf3-40c4-ad02-04e5b9e5fd24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** profanity-laced jeers, and thumbs-down gestures from roughly 3,500 attendees at the NYPD's National Night Out Against Crime event on Staten Island's Midland Beach boardwalk Tuesday night. Rand Paul's Senate Homeland Security Committee **[is set to vote Thursday](https://substack.com/redirect/c72b8a25-0319-428f-a83d-6b8901542dad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on holding Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress after Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment more than 100 times during last week's hearing rather than answering questions about COVID's origins, gain-of-function research, and pandemic policy decisions.

# **White House launches "Fraud Ledger" website to track Anti-Fraud Task Force results**
The White House unveiled **[a new public website](https://substack.com/redirect/194d95c7-e9f1-4119-ad4d-89efdd6a7c32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** called "The Fraud Ledger" Tuesday, designed to document the findings of Vice President JD Vance's Task Force to Eliminate Fraud.
* **The site tracks three metrics:** fraud uncovered through data analysis, fraud stopped in real annual spending, and fraud enforcement through indictments and settlements. Since January 2025, the task force claims to have uncovered $229.9 billion in total fraud.

* **The Small Business Administration tops the list with $122.9 billion in uncovered fraud,** followed by Health and Human Services at $96.2 billion and the Department of Labor at $7 billion. The task force says it has stopped $56.4 billion in annual fraudulent spending and enforced $55.5 billion through legal actions. Medicaid fraud deferrals include over $2 billion from California and $500 million from Minnesota.
* **Vance is simultaneously pushing Congress to codify anti-fraud measures** into law, arguing the effort should outlast the current administration.

Growing up in Allagash and spending years working 80-hour weeks in the woods to make ends meet, I know firsthand what working Mainers need from our government.
And for 30 years, Susan Collins has failed us. Time and again, she has sold us out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. And I’m sick of it.
My name is Troy Jackson. I’m a proud Mainer, father, and fifth-generation logger.
This weekend, I officially earned the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate. Now it’s time to defeat Susan Collins and her billionaire backers. So I’m asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to become a Founding Donor to my campaign right now and help us win the most important Senate race in the country. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jackson]
DONATE TO DEFEAT SUSAN COLLINS AND FLIP THE SENATE! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jackson]
Let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me.
When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us.
After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that nothing would change unless there were working-class voices in power.
So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people.
I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.
I’m building this campaign the right way. With grassroots support from folks like you. I’m not running to impress the billionaires or the corporate class. I’m running for the mom who’s worried about how she’ll fill her gas tank this week. I’m running for the kid whose whole life will be determined by the quality of his education. I’m running to ensure every working family in Maine has the government they deserve.
If you believe in this fight and our movement, I’m humbly asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild today to help us reach our fundraising goal and take on the GOP’s millions. Even $10, $25, or $50 makes a difference >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jackson]

# Let's Rock the Vote!
---
| | | _To our Friends and Supporters, _ It's hard to believe it’s been 10 months since we launched this campaign, and that our next milestone - the primary election - is just days away. I’ve already been gratified by the number of people our team and I run into who let us know they plan to vote for this campaign, and how many have already done that by voting early. Thank you! The outcome of this primary election will also determine who will be our Democratic candidate for Governor. And it will determine which of us candidates for Congress will move on to the general election in November. And here in Northern Wisconsin, we’ll be doing our part to help elect a US Congress that represents people not corporations, and that once again does its job, following the Constitution as a co-equal branch of government. There’s a lot at stake in this primary election and the voters I talk to across the political spectrum are most definitely paying attention. **Please remember to vote on Tuesday August 11th.** And if there’s any chance I haven’t asked you before, I would love to have your support!
---
---
| | | Fred
---
---
Here's a picture from my old State Legislature days with a few of the best volunteers in Wisconsin!
---
| | | PS: On Election Day, remember that you can register at your polling location. And although the polls close at 8pm, you are entitled to cast your vote if you are in line by that time.
---
|
---
# **_On the Road_**
---
| | |
---
| | | **At the Hmong American Festival** Fred enjoyed meeting people from the Hmong community around Wisconsin at Saturday's Hmong Wausau Festival. Many thanks to Yee Leng Xiong and other Hmong leaders for organizing this incredible event.
---
| | |
---
| | | The story of Wisconsin's Hmong community and their arrival in Wisconsin beginning during the Vietnam War in the 1970's is a story of heroism, resilience, and family values. Since that time, with a lot of community support, and sometimes in the face of persecution and discrimination, Hmong families have created a thriving culture centered in and around Wausau. Fred looks forward to serving and continuing to learn from members of the Hmong community in Congress next year.
---
| | | **A Town Hall in Delta, WI** One of Team Clark’s last Town Halls before the primary took place in Delta, WI last Wednesday. Sjana and other local residents hosted Fred for a night of engaging conversation and important questions.We learn the most when people from every political leaning are in the room — and that was true for this event.
---
---
| |
---
Both during the town hall and in conversations afterward, one theme kept coming up: affordability. Whether it was a question about how to fix our healthcare system, or how a small town is supposed to find $200,000 for a dump truck to plow next winter's snow — the question underneath it all was the same: how do we make sure Wisconsin families can afford the basics — healthcare, safe roads, reliable services — and still have room to get ahead? Fred will keep showing up in small towns, cities, and villages across this district. Because in Congress, he plans to represent all the people of the 7th CD.
---
| | | **Wisconsin Valley Fair** The Wisconsin Valley Fair at Marathon Park in Wausau is one of the most scenic county fair locations anywhere and it attracts people from all over central Wisconsin and beyond.Team Clark had a chance to visit on Wednesday, spending time with visitors in the exhibition barns and on the midway. If you’re going this year of course you'll want to check out the livestock barns and see the 4H youth at work proudly showing their calves, pigs, sheep, chickens and more.Then, make sure to check out the cheese curds from the Wausau Breakfast Optimists. You won’t find better anywhere else! Next - we strongly suggest checking out the nearby homemade pie stand run each year by the First English Lutheran Church of Wausau and their volunteers. Blueberry, Raspberry, Apple and more, all with ice cream, and reportedly baked by Amish bakers using wood-fired ovens. They’re awesome pies! And their tent is a great place to get out of the sun and talk with voters. Pie and politics - it’s a natural fit!
---
---
| |
---
---
| | |
# **In the News**
---
| | | **Tom Tiffany’s Assault on the Apostle Islands** Fred visited Sand Island on Monday, one of the 21 islands that make up the Apostle Islands National Lakeshore. The Apostles are a crown jewel of Wisconsin's outdoor heritage.But Tom Tiffany wants to downgrade the protection for Sand Island, a step that would lead to future private development.
---
| | |
---
Nobody at home thinks this is a good idea, and Tom Tiffany has never once shown up publicly to explain to the people around Bayfield, Red Cliff, and nearby communities why he knows better than every other local community leader who has opposed his proposal. It's long past time for new representation in Congress for northern Wisconsin, including our Lake Superior region.
---
| | |
---

| | | **Do You Have a Plan to Vote?** As you know, we have a primary election on Tuesday, August 11th! We are confident that with your support, we will pass through the primary and use the momentum to carry us to November. But to ensure a smooth election day, we want to provide you with all the information you need to create a plan to vote. To check if you are registered, you can go to myvote.wi.gov. By entering your name and birthday, you can find your registration status and polling location and request an absentee ballot.In-person absentee (early) voting runs from July 28th through August 9th. You can drop your ballot off or fill one out at your municipal clerk’s office, or at another designated in your town. Check myvote.wi.gov for precise locations for early voting.You may cast your ballot on Election Day if you are in line by 8pm. And you can always register to vote at your polling location on Election Day.For the full list of deadlines, check myvote.wi.gov/en-us/Voter-Deadlines. Voting is best done early and with a plan in mind. By voting, you are participating in your democracy and exercising a right so rare in the history of humanity. Each vote cast is a quiet commitment to our republic, and an act of personal courage and patriotism. Let’s go win this election together!

I’ve already been gratified by the number of people our team and I run into who let us know they plan to vote for this campaign, and how many have already done that by voting early. Thank you! The outcome of this primary election will also determine who will be our Democratic candidate for Governor. And it will determine which of us candidates for Congress will move on to the general election in November. And here in Northern Wisconsin, we’ll be doing our part to help elect a US Congress that represents people not corporations, and that once again does its job, following the Constitution as a co-equal branch of government. There’s a lot at stake in this primary election and the voters I talk to across the political spectrum are most definitely paying attention. Please remember to vote on Tuesday August 11th. And if there’s any chance I haven’t asked you before, I would love to have your support! | | | Fred Here's a picture from my old State Legislature days with a few of the best volunteers in Wisconsin! | | | PS: On Election Day, remember that you can register at your polling location. And although the polls close at 8pm, you are entitled to cast your vote if you are in line by that time. | On the Road | | | | | | At the Hmong American Festival Fred enjoyed meeting people from the Hmong community around Wisconsin at Saturday's Hmong Wausau Festival. Many thanks to Yee Leng Xiong and other Hmong leaders for organizing this incredible event. | | | | | | The story of Wisconsin's Hmong community and their arrival in Wisconsin beginning during the Vietnam War in the 1970's is a story of heroism, resilience, and family values. Since that time, with a lot of community support, and sometimes in the face of persecution and discrimination, Hmong families have created a thriving culture centered in and around Wausau. Fred looks forward to serving and continuing to learn from members of the Hmong community in Congress next year. | | | A Town Hall in Delta, WI One of Team Clark’s last Town Halls before the primary took place in Delta, WI last Wednesday. Sjana and other local residents hosted Fred for a night of engaging conversation and important questions.We learn the most when people from every political leaning are in the room — and that was true for this event. | | Both during the town hall and in conversations afterward, one theme kept coming up: affordability. Whether it was a question about how to fix our healthcare system, or how a small town is supposed to find $200,000 for a dump truck to plow next winter's snow — the question underneath it all was the same: how do we make sure Wisconsin families can afford the basics — healthcare, safe roads, reliable services — and still have room to get ahead? Fred will keep showing up in small towns, cities, and villages across this district. Because in Congress, he plans to represent all the people of the 7th CD. | | | Wisconsin Valley Fair The Wisconsin Valley Fair at Marathon Park in Wausau is one of the most scenic county fair locations anywhere and it attracts people from all over central Wisconsin and beyond.Team Clark had a chance to visit on Wednesday, spending time with visitors in the exhibition barns and on the midway. If you’re going this year of course you'll want to check out the livestock barns and see the 4H youth at work proudly showing their calves, pigs, sheep, chickens and more.Then, make sure to check out the cheese curds from the Wausau Breakfast Optimists. You won’t find better anywhere else! Next - we strongly suggest checking out the nearby homemade pie stand run each year by the First English Lutheran Church of Wausau and their volunteers. Blueberry, Raspberry, Apple and more, all with ice cream, and reportedly baked by Amish bakers using wood-fired ovens. They’re awesome pies! And their tent is a great place to get out of the sun and talk with voters. Pie and politics - it’s a natural fit! | | | | | In the News | | | Tom Tiffany’s Assault on the Apostle Islands Fred visited Sand Island on Monday, one of the 21 islands that make up the Apostle Islands National Lakeshore. The Apostles are a crown jewel of Wisconsin's outdoor heritage.But Tom Tiffany wants to downgrade the protection for Sand Island, a step that would lead to future private development. | | | Nobody at home thinks this is a good idea, and Tom Tiffany has never once shown up publicly to explain to the people around Bayfield, Red Cliff, and nearby communities why he knows better than every other local community leader who has opposed his proposal. It's long past time for new representation in Congress for northern Wisconsin, including our Lake Superior region. | | | Join Us for a Good Old Fashioned Phone Bank We will hold biweekly phone banking sessions on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 6-7pm. These sessions will also teach you how to conduct a phone bank if you are new to it. If you already know how to phone bank, please join us and we will get you started on making calls for Fred. But to ensure a smooth election day, we want to provide you with all the information you need to create a plan to vote. To check if you are registered, you can go to myvote.wi.gov. By entering your name and birthday, you can find your registration status and polling location and request an absentee ballot.In-person absentee (early) voting runs from July 28th through August 9th. ### Aitken Campaign Highlights Grassroots Momentum as Opponent Relies on Boston "Power Brokers"

Republican Bristol County DA candidate Seth Aitken draws a sharp contrast between his community-driven campaign and his opponent's reliance on political insiders.
SWANSEA, MA - AUGUST 6, 2026 -- Seth Aitken, the Republican candidate for Bristol County District Attorney, issued a statement today addressing the news that former Governor Charlie Baker and former Lt. Governor Karyn Polito will headline a Boston-based fundraiser for his opponent, Democratic State Representative Chris Markey, on August 13.
Aitken embraced the announcement, characterizing Markey's reliance on high-profile Boston political figures as a sign that his own campaign's grassroots message of independent, community-focused leadership is successfully resonating with voters across Bristol County.
"My opponent's decision to seek out this endorsement from old political allies is evidence that he is genuinely concerned about the challenge in front of him," Aitken said. "He sees how my campaign is resonating with so many voters who are tired of entrenched career politicians doing the bidding of a self-serving political machine. I take it as a compliment."
Aitken, a former assistant district attorney and Fall River City Administrator, is running to modernize the DA's office and deliver fresh leadership following the upcoming retirement of incumbent Thomas Quinn III. Rejecting the traditional playbook of courting state party elites, Aitken noted that a truly independent prosecutor must answer only to the community, not the political establishment. " Unlike Mr. Markey, I am not seeking the support of political insiders or Boston power brokers--I'm asking for the support of the people I'm running to serve: the people of Bristol County," Aitken continued.
The Aitken campaign is focused on mobilizing everyday residents who want a prosecutor unbeholden to the state's political machine, centering its platform on accountability, fairness, and public safety.
"This campaign belongs to the voters of Bristol County: working families, parents, seniors, small-business owners, and everyday residents," Aitken said. "Our campaign will be built by ordinary people, one conversation and one contribution at a time. We don't have a political machine. We have something better: the heart, trust, and determination of this community. Together, we can defeat the insiders and deliver the leadership Bristol County deserves." For more information on Seth Aitken's campaign for Bristol County District Attorney, or to find out how to get involved, please visit Aitken4DA.com.
###
Seth Aitken is a Fall River attorney licensed in Massachusetts state and federal courts, with a diverse legal background as an Assistant District Attorney, criminal defense attorney, and city administrator. His experience includes criminal law, municipal law, real estate, probate, and civil litigation. He previously served eight years in the U.S. Army. He resides in Swansea with his wife and three sons.

clean_body: | | | | | | | == | NOTE: The following Press Release is being distributed for Seth Aitken, candidate for District Attorney in Bristol County. | | | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE CONTACT: Libby Reilly PHONE: (251) 366-9900 EMAIL: mailto:info@aitken4da.com Aitken Campaign Highlights Grassroots Momentum as Opponent Relies on Boston "Power Brokers" Republican Bristol County DA candidate Seth Aitken draws a sharp contrast between his community-driven campaign and his opponent's reliance on political insiders. SWANSEA, MA - AUGUST 6, 2026 -- Seth Aitken, the Republican candidate for Bristol County District Attorney, issued a statement today addressing the news that former Governor Charlie Baker and former Lt. Governor Karyn Polito will headline a Boston-based fundraiser for his opponent, Democratic State Representative Chris Markey, on August 13. Aitken embraced the announcement, characterizing Markey's reliance on high-profile Boston political figures as a sign that his own campaign's grassroots message of independent, community-focused leadership is successfully resonating with voters across Bristol County. "My opponent's decision to seek out this endorsement from old political allies is evidence that he is genuinely concerned about the challenge in front of him," Aitken said. "He sees how my campaign is resonating with so many voters who are tired of entrenched career politicians doing the bidding of a self-serving political machine. I take it as a compliment." Aitken, a former assistant district attorney and Fall River City Administrator, is running to modernize the DA's office and deliver fresh leadership following the upcoming retirement of incumbent Thomas Quinn III. Rejecting the traditional playbook of courting state party elites, Aitken noted that a truly independent prosecutor must answer only to the community, not the political establishment. " Unlike Mr. Markey, I am not seeking the support of political insiders or Boston power brokers--I'm asking for the support of the people I'm running to serve: the people of Bristol County," Aitken continued. The Aitken campaign is focused on mobilizing everyday residents who want a prosecutor unbeholden to the state's political machine, centering its platform on accountability, fairness, and public safety. "This campaign belongs to the voters of Bristol County: working families, parents, seniors, small-business owners, and everyday residents," Aitken said. "Our campaign will be built by ordinary people, one conversation and one contribution at a time. We don't have a political machine. We have something better: the heart, trust, and determination of this community. Together, we can defeat the insiders and deliver the leadership Bristol County deserves." For more information on Seth Aitken's campaign for Bristol County District Attorney, or to find out how to get involved, please visit Aitken4DA.com. Seth Aitken is a Fall River attorney licensed in Massachusetts state and federal courts, with a diverse legal background as an Assistant District Attorney, criminal defense attorney, and city administrator. His experience includes criminal law, municipal law, real estate, probate, and civil litigation. He previously served eight years in the U.S. Army. name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: 61 years ago today
body:
61 years ago today, the Voting Rights Act was signed into law.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
61 years ago today, the Voting Rights Act was signed into law. It was a monumental victory won through the courage of civil rights leaders who risked everything for the fundamental right to vote.
Yet today, voting rights remain under direct attack across our country and _especially_ right here in Texas.
Last year, my Democratic colleagues in the Texas House and I stood up to fight back against Greg Abbott and Texas Republicans when they pushed corrupt mid-decade redistricting. We broke quorum, halted legislative business, and put a national spotlight on Abbott’s downright corrupt plan to redraw district lines, add extra GOP seats, and dilute the voting power of Black and Latino communities.
But despite our bravery, the Supreme Court cleared the way for Republicans' rigged maps to be approved. Then, they gutted key protections of the Voting Rights Act.
But Abbott isn't done, Peter. He, along with other Texas Republicans, has already promised to come back next year and rig the maps all over again. And they’re already eyeing when Texas gains 4-5 more seats by the end of this decade.
So, if we don’t elect a governor committed to vetoing unfair maps this fall, millions of Texans risk losing fair representation for a generation.
**[Will you chip in $5 to help me defeat Greg Abbott and defend voting rights in Texas?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260806_1_vra.xDp6P4&refcode=em20260806-1756&amount=5&t=1&akid=1756%2E299639%2ErCyHZx)**

Thank you,
Gina

subject: Help stop Trump's USPS Board nominations

body:
Why do we need to stop Trump's nominees?
A FedEx-linked Postmaster General already runs USPS . Add a board dominated by Trump’s corporate insider donor appointees poised to keep slowing the mail and raising prices, consolidating post offices, and outsourcing work toward privatization, and you have a recipe for disaster.
Public pressure has helped stop attacks on the USPS in the past. A federal judge just put a temporary stop on Trump turning USPS into his election administrator , blocking ballots from anyone not on a Homeland Security citizenship list. We can win here, too.
Stop Trump’s USPS takeover by demanding the Senate reject the Postal Board of Governors nominees now >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-trumps-postal-board-takeover/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
START WRITING NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-trumps-postal-board-takeover/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Team,
Donald Trump recently nominated four candidates for the USPS Board of Governors in an attempted takeover of the cherished public institution that is older than the nation itself. And he knows good and well USPS is responsible for carrying millions of ballots during the midterm elections.
The Postal Board controls the policy decisions, financials, service standards, and long-term direction of USPS. It also has sole hire and fire power over the Postmaster General.
Our coalition made enough noise that two of the nominees never made it to a vote , but the other two – Jeffrey Brodsky and William Gallo – were just voted out of committee and the entire Senate could soon vote to confirm or reject them.
This is our last chance to stop Trump from dominating the postal board and being able to bully a giant step forward on his election interference schemes, as well as everything from price hikes and delivery slowdowns to privatization.
Demand the Senate reject these disastrous nominees while we still can >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-trumps-postal-board-takeover/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
START WRITING NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-trumps-postal-board-takeover/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
Rural communities, Indigenous communities, seniors, veterans, small businesses, postal workers, and voters shouldn’t pay the price while private shipping corporations claim the profitable pieces. But that's exactly what these guys want.
Brodsky has spent 30 years in the corporate restructuring world, treating distressed companies as projects to be cut apart, reorganized, and squeezed for investors — a literal privatization expert. Gallo comes from commodities trading and private business. Neither one has any postal experience or much less a record of defending universal service, postal workers, affordable rates, rural delivery, or election mail.
We have no reason to believe anything other than these corporate stooges are ready and willing to do whatever Trump wants regardless of the impact on one of the most trusted, effective, and respected public services in the country.
A Trump-dominated board will almost certainly weaken protections for election mail , putting vote by mail at risk for the midterms and beyond.
Trump wants a Postal Service that follows his political orders and prepares itself for a corporate sell-off. The Senate can stop him. Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.

It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

name: Defenders of Wildlife
subject: Heroes in American Conservation: Explore the Spirit of the Wilderness with Olaus Murie
body:
Meet American Conservation Hero Olaus Murie
Meet American Conservation Hero Olaus Murie
| [](https://support.defenders.org/s/5854785/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
|
---
[](https://support.defenders.org/s/5854786/38SyG9Xl)
---
#
Meet American Conservation Hero Olaus Murie
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Who is he?_**
Olaus Murie (1889–1963) was a naturalist and wildlife biologist. A bit of a black sheep while at the U.S. Biological Survey (today’s U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service), he championed the importance of maintaining a healthy predator-prey balance in an ecosystem.
#
Murie spent six years conducting field research on caribou in Alaska. During these studies, he came to believe that natural predation by wolves was healthy for the herd. These findings and subsequent work led him to be increasingly outspoken against predator extermination, especially later in his career.
#
_Murie’s wife, Mardy, accompanied Olaus and is also a “conservation hero.” Be sure to check out our upcoming American Conservation Heroes installment to learn about her!_
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_What did Olaus do to help protect wildlife?_**
Murie spent over a decade studying the Jackson Hole elk herd in Wyoming, observing how healthy habitat and ample space to spread out were essential to their survival. This later inspired him to help create Jackson Hole National Monument (now part of Grand Teton National Park) to establish a larger, natural habitat boundary for elk. He also advocated for the expansion of the what is now Olympic National Park, to include the natural boundaries of the Bogachiel and Hoh River valleys’ rainforests.
#
Later in life, the Muries both returned to Alaska in a campaign to protect what is now the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. They looked to preserve the entire ecosystem — some 8 million acres at the time, later expanded to 19 million —which marked a new generation of larger national parks and refuges.
#
Today the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge is under threat from administration policies as well as warming temperatures. Defenders of Wildlife is advocating for the continued protection of this vital habitat, including [**preventing oil and gas lease sales**](https://support.defenders.org/s/5854787/38SyG9Xl) and taking steps to reduce carbon emissions to protect valuable, icy homes for [**a variety of animals.**](https://support.defenders.org/s/5854788/38SyG9Xl)
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_How can you become a conservation hero?_**
Speak up for nature! [**Learn and share the do’s and don’ts when exploring wild places**](https://support.defenders.org/s/5854789/38SyG9Xl) with your friends and family. You can also [**become a Wildlife Defender**](https://support.defenders.org/s/5854790/38SyG9Xl) to join a growing grassroots community that speaks up for nature across the nation.
#
|
---
###
_A note on our Heroes in American Conservation series: Our country has a long and complex history, populated with high-profile figures whose views may have been complicated or divisive in their time as well as ours. We present these conservationists in the interest of creating a greater understanding of the roots of the American conservation movement, and to inspire you to make your own contribution to ongoing conversations about how we preserve our wild world._
#

---

name: Raja K.
subject: I won’t be on the ballot…
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
For the first time in nearly a decade, I won't be on the ballot this November.
I'll be honest — that's a strange thing to sit with. For years, asking for your vote has been how I showed up in this fight. This year, that's not an option for me.
But here's what hasn't changed: I am not going anywhere.
I started Equal Opportunity Now because I refuse to sit on the sidelines while Donald Trump and his MAGA allies try to dismantle everything that made my family's story possible. Not being on the ballot doesn't change that belief. If anything, it's freed me up to do something I care about just as much: help elect the next generation of Democrats who will fight for working families and take back power from MAGA extremists.
That's not just a talking point. This month alone, Equal Opportunity Now is putting $100,000 directly into the hands of Democratic candidates and causes — in Illinois and around the country. We're doing it because I know firsthand what it takes to run a campaign, and I know how much difference an early, real investment can make for a candidate who's ready to fight but needs the resources to do it.
I've spent my career fighting for fair wages, for a democracy that works for everyone, for an economy where hard work still leads somewhere. I'm not done fighting for any of that just because my name isn't on a ballot this year. If anything, I'm just getting started in a new way — finding the leaders who will carry this fight forward, and making sure they have what they need to win.
Will you chip in $25 or $50 to Equal Opportunity Now today to help us keep building? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email&amount=25]
DONATE » [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email?amount=25]
My name may not be on the ballot. But I'm still all in.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi
Founder | Equal Opportunity Now

Peter,
The unthinkable is happening before our very eyes.
For years Nebraska's 1st Congressional District, currently represented by ultra-MAGA extremist Congressman Mike Flood (R-NE), has been written off and labeled unwinnable for Democrats. As of Wednesday, this is no longer the case.
In a seismic shift, the DCCC, the campaign arm for House Democrats, just announced that Nebraska's 1st Congressional District is now part of their "districts in play," a program for districts seen as highly competitive.
---
| [](https://eeuwd7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0017VEFq6gYDuL8nsE19Yh0JnVdnVGAvuj09auNBmcsHDsjQFUQzRxol60lFF6VXiTQ1IXZn0lFzo1porVFo0q8DMET8Pm5cuZSH2OCkdXp0oMnQKYhhfNdHxbnRzKZfLeIprc4K09Cbxo_krljAQ6imD5q1_A9WeTncEdpL5rcB4tRdwuGoOssnjKmyOZNomKvdvGBaiigdt0JsLdZOONvoA_87dF0BJsI&c=KoNlPnjcTz45YQJqgiFknAXigue7MRvY5VPuYPEU0U9xb328IUH7DA==&ch=eQ2IjOZhbbWoAfxznnq3r1mJFtCU_8Hzfg2-wfAVIhtImPVPS97tSA==)

To the Congressman's credit he is one of the only GOP representatives in the nation to host public town halls across his district. But the beautiful thing is that at every single town hall he's hosted constituents show up en masse to absolutely obliterate him.
In many cases 400+ constituents will show up to heckle, boo, and ask cutting questions that expose his betrayal of working Nebraskans.
But this district's competitiveness stems from more than just Flood's unpopularity. The reason why this race is in play is because of the caliber of his opponent:
Chris Backemeyer, a 21-year career civil servant with the US State Department, who saw firsthand the impact of MAGA's efforts to undermine the federal workforce.
A year ago this race, and a state like Nebraska for that matter, were considered unwinnable. Yet thanks to the hard work of Democrats across Nebraska and across the nation -- no red district or red state is out of reach for us. When we organize everywhere we can win anywhere.

This election is all about records.

Derek, this election here in battleground Pennsylvania is all about records. Which candidate has a record of results? A record of progress? A record of getting sh*t done? But I’ve gotta be honest. There’s another kind of record that might be my favorite: **43-0.** I went to court against Donald Trump and his allies 43 times to protect Pennsylvanians’ votes in the 2020 election. **I wasn’t going to let Donald Trump score a single victory over the good people of Pennsylvania or undermine your fundamental right to vote – and I didn’t.** 43 wins. #### _**E[ndless Urgency exists for one reason: to cut through the noise and focus on the conversations that actually matter. It's free to read because these ideas should be accessible to everyone--but it only exists because readers choose to support it. If you believe we need more honest conversations and fewer manufactured distractions, become a paid subscriber. Just $8/month makes a huge difference.](https://substack.com/redirect/f6a14408-e6bc-4fe1-8004-609c3d2bb925?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/f6a14408-e6bc-4fe1-8004-609c3d2bb925?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
I'm in New York this week doing a ton of media, which means I've spent a lot of time talking about the serious and genuinely disgusting allegations against Max Miller. One of those stops was Piers Morgan's YouTube show.
If you've ever watched me on Piers Morgan, you already know the drill. At some point -- no matter what I was actually invited on to discuss -- Piers is going to blow up the entire segment so he can, once again, complain about transgender athletes in women's sports. Then he and his guests get to yell at me about it and act like I'm the weirdo, when they're the ones who cannot stop obsessing over this stuff.
And that's exactly the point. Every conversation gets dragged back to the same, stale, handful of culture-war fights--even when we're supposed to be talking about something else entirely.
The two conservatives screaming at me yesterday about trans kids love to lecture Democrats like me about keeping women safe. Women's safety, they tell me, is sacred. That it is the defining issue of our time.
And yet -- when an actual woman or child is harmed? When the abuse isn't hypothetical, but sitting right in front of them (sometimes at the same dinner table)? Suddenly they're nowhere to be found. Max Miller breaking his toddler daughter's collarbone. The violence against his ex-wife and his daughter. A disgusting public display of a man attacking his own family, and a Republican Party that just turns a blind eye. The President of the United States calling Max Miller "a good man." The Speaker of the House working to guarantee his reelection anyway. On all of that? Silence.
Most of them have nothing to say about Epstein either -- or about what it implies about Donald Trump and so much of the billionaire class tangled up in the trafficking and abuse of little girls. One of the panelists on Piers, Clay Travis, once sat across from me and literally questioned whether the Epstein survivors are survivors of any crime at all.
So it begs the question: why are these people so obsessed with shitting on trans kids, and so completely uninterested in the very real abuse happening in this country -- abuse committed by Republican politicians and influencers against women? Why won't the Republican Party police its own? Why is there an ocean of outrage for the one thing and not a single drop for the other?
Because if you're arguing about bathrooms, you're not asking why the people screaming loudest about protecting women and children never seem interested when women and children are actually harmed.
The answer is isn't complicated. It's profitable: They're scoring cheap political points. They know most people don't understand the lived experience of transgender Americans, and that fear is easy to exploit. They know it polls badly for Democrats -- I get it, I recognize the politics. But I am not going to attack trans kids who want the same thing every kid wants: to feel safe and to belong. That's what this is actually about. Beyond that, I think individual sports leagues are perfectly capable of deciding who plays in their sport, and the federal government has no business in it. Piers and the rest hate that answer -- because for all their small-government cosplay, they very obviously want to use the full power of the state to force their will on everyone.
* * *
#### **[If you're tired of the outrage machine deciding what everyone talks about, help us build something different. Endless Urgency stays free because paid subscribers make it possible. If this work has been valuable to you, becoming a subscriber for just $8/month helps keep it that way.](https://substack.com/redirect/f6a14408-e6bc-4fe1-8004-609c3d2bb925?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/f6a14408-e6bc-4fe1-8004-609c3d2bb925?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
But back to the real point, because this comes down to two things.
First: There is an entire political class and media ecosystem whose success depends on keeping us--fellow citizens, neighbors, even family members--at each other's throats instead of asking what _they 're_ actually doing. They manufacture stories about the people we're told to fear -- trans kids, gay people, minorities -- because our hatred is their business model. The social platforms pay them for the most salacious content they can produce. And all of it is a magic trick, designed to pull your eyes away from the actual theft happening in this economy. We are living through the single largest transfer of wealth in the history of this country -- out of the pockets of the poor and the working class and straight into the accounts of billionaires like Donald Trump. As long as we're screaming at each other about trans issues -- which matter, but affect a genuinely tiny number of people -- they get to keep robbing us blind.
Second: and here's the crazy part--they still think this _works_. They still think it wins elections. In their minds, this is what beat Kamala Harris in 2024 -- that infamous "they/them" ad.
But they've never understood why that ad worked. They spent so much time measuring the ad that they never bothered to understand the frustration underneath it. Which is why they've run some version of it in nearly every race since Trump took office. And they have almost uniformly lost.
Look at the Omaha mayor's race, where Republicans went all in attacking the Democrat on trans issues -- and got answered with a simple, devastating message: these guys care more about bathrooms than they do about fixing your potholes. That's it. Be responsive to what people actually need. Drag the conversation back to where people actually are: trying to survive an economy Donald Trump has decimated. That's how you beat this, every single time.
So I'm sick of it -- but I'll keep going on the shows, because you all know my rule: I'll talk to anybody about anything, and I'll make my case. They think they're scoring an own goal on me every time they pull this. It just reads as pathetic, because that's what it is. It's sad. No new ideas. No new messaging. A president losing his mind. A party that can't even locate Mitch McConnell. This entire MAGA movement is falling apart, and all they've got left is manufactured outrage about trans athletes and Fauci's journal and whatever else the right-wing echo chamber cooked up this week.
They've got nothing for the real things. They're not angry that Donald Trump is stealing from the American people. They're not angry that Max Miller broke his daughter's collarbone. They're not angry about an economy that's crushing the very people they claim to represent.
They're angry wherever the algorithm tells them to be angry next.
And that's the whole scam. Keep people fighting each other long enough that nobody asks what the people in power are actually doing.
But they don't get it. And honestly? I hope they keep handing themselves the rope.
Because every time they try to change the subject, they remind people they don't actually have an answer for the problems keeping myself or my fellow Americans up at night.
So I'll keep showing up. I'll keep dragging the conversation back to what actually matters. And every time they try to change the subject, I'll remind them why they wanted to change it in the first place.

Eyes on the ball, folks.
With urgency,
--Mike

clean_body: Endless Urgency exists for one reason: to cut through the noise and focus on the conversations that actually matter. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? | | | Aug 6 | | | | | | | | | | | | E I'm in New York this week doing a ton of media, which means I've spent a lot of time talking about the serious and genuinely disgusting allegations against Max Miller. One of those stops was Piers Morgan's YouTube show. If you've ever watched me on Piers Morgan, you already know the drill. At some point -- no matter what I was actually invited on to discuss -- Piers is going to blow up the entire segment so he can, once again, complain about transgender athletes in women's sports. Then he and his guests get to yell at me about it and act like I'm the weirdo, when they're the ones who cannot stop obsessing over this stuff. And that's exactly the point. Every conversation gets dragged back to the same, stale, handful of culture-war fights--even when we're supposed to be talking about something else entirely. The two conservatives screaming at me yesterday about trans kids love to lecture Democrats like me about keeping women safe. Women's safety, they tell me, is sacred. That it is the defining issue of our time. And yet -- when an actual woman or child is harmed? When the abuse isn't hypothetical, but sitting right in front of them (sometimes at the same dinner table)? Suddenly they're nowhere to be found. Max Miller breaking his toddler daughter's collarbone. The violence against his ex-wife and his daughter. A disgusting public display of a man attacking his own family, and a Republican Party that just turns a blind eye. The President of the United States calling Max Miller "a good man." The Speaker of the House working to guarantee his reelection anyway. On all of that? Silence. Most of them have nothing to say about Epstein either -- or about what it implies about Donald Trump and so much of the billionaire class tangled up in the trafficking and abuse of little girls. One of the panelists on Piers, Clay Travis, once sat across from me and literally questioned whether the Epstein survivors are survivors of any crime at all. So it begs the question: why are these people so obsessed with shitting on trans kids, and so completely uninterested in the very real abuse happening in this country -- abuse committed by Republican politicians and influencers against women? Why won't the Republican Party police its own? Why is there an ocean of outrage for the one thing and not a single drop for the other? Because if you're arguing about bathrooms, you're not asking why the people screaming loudest about protecting women and children never seem interested when women and children are actually harmed. The answer is isn't complicated. It's profitable: They're scoring cheap political points. They know most people don't understand the lived experience of transgender Americans, and that fear is easy to exploit. They know it polls badly for Democrats -- I get it, I recognize the politics. But I am not going to attack trans kids who want the same thing every kid wants: to feel safe and to belong. That's what this is actually about. Beyond that, I think individual sports leagues are perfectly capable of deciding who plays in their sport, and the federal government has no business in it. Piers and the rest hate that answer -- because for all their small-government cosplay, they very obviously want to use the full power of the state to force their will on everyone. * But back to the real point, because this comes down to two things. First: There is an entire political class and media ecosystem whose success depends on keeping us--fellow citizens, neighbors, even family members--at each other's throats instead of asking what they 're actually doing. They manufacture stories about the people we're told to fear -- trans kids, gay people, minorities -- because our hatred is their business model. The social platforms pay them for the most salacious content they can produce. And all of it is a magic trick, designed to pull your eyes away from the actual theft happening in this economy. We are living through the single largest transfer of wealth in the history of this country -- out of the pockets of the poor and the working class and straight into the accounts of billionaires like Donald Trump. As long as we're screaming at each other about trans issues -- which matter, but affect a genuinely tiny number of people -- they get to keep robbing us blind. Second: and here's the crazy part--they still think this works. They still think it wins elections. In their minds, this is what beat Kamala Harris in 2024 -- that infamous "they/them" ad. But they've never understood why that ad worked. They spent so much time measuring the ad that they never bothered to understand the frustration underneath it. Which is why they've run some version of it in nearly every race since Trump took office. And they have almost uniformly lost. Look at the Omaha mayor's race, where Republicans went all in attacking the Democrat on trans issues -- and got answered with a simple, devastating message: these guys care more about bathrooms than they do about fixing your potholes. That's it. Be responsive to what people actually need. Drag the conversation back to where people actually are: trying to survive an economy Donald Trump has decimated. That's how you beat this, every single time. So I'm sick of it -- but I'll keep going on the shows, because you all know my rule: I'll talk to anybody about anything, and I'll make my case. They think they're scoring an own goal on me every time they pull this. It just reads as pathetic, because that's what it is. It's sad. No new ideas. No new messaging. A president losing his mind. A party that can't even locate Mitch McConnell. This entire MAGA movement is falling apart, and all they've got left is manufactured outrage about trans athletes and Fauci's journal and whatever else the right-wing echo chamber cooked up this week. They've got nothing for the real things. They're not angry that Donald Trump is stealing from the American people. They're not angry that Max Miller broke his daughter's collarbone. They're not angry about an economy that's crushing the very people they claim to represent. They're angry wherever the algorithm tells them to be angry next. And that's the whole scam. Keep people fighting each other long enough that nobody asks what the people in power are actually doing. But they don't get it. And honestly? I hope they keep handing themselves the rope. Because every time they try to change the subject, they remind people they don't actually have an answer for the problems keeping myself or my fellow Americans up at night. So I'll keep showing up. I'll keep dragging the conversation back to what actually matters. And every time they try to change the subject, I'll remind them why they wanted to change it in the first place. Eyes on the ball, folks. With urgency, --Mike Mike Nellis is a Democratic strategist and entrepreneur who has raised over $1 billion for Democratic campaigns and causes. Join the DNC, New Disabled South Rising, and the College Democrats of America Disability Caucus for a training call on voting rights for people with disabilities and poll workers. As the Trump administration relies on public unawareness to threaten our fundamental voting rights, we must unite to learn about our rights to accessibility accommodations, poll worker assistance, mail-in voting, and private, independent voting.
**JOIN US TO:**
* Learn about your voting rights and how you can support people with disabilities at the polls;
* Hear from community members who have had their rights threatened;
* Find out how to get more engaged in voter protection.

**EVENT DETAILS : **
* **Date** : Monday, August 10, 2026
* **Time** : 6:30 PM PT

Your participation is critical to the DNC’s mission to fight back against injustice and protect voting rights throughout America.
