Fellow Conservative,

If you haven’t heard about “See You at the Library Day” on Fox News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources,
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjB9AAwAAAAAAi9Ul8vQTO4CAjlpWH2fr0R7zqx-k46v1UdKQuWuc4fO__fAVxEhIpcxYRpd34LP2dLGvV4ucFgpImIDrwN5eexriXCAmWwRf4TiWumxjA
please let me tell you why it’s so critical.

Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian.

She would fill your mind with classics like Pat the Bunny and The Little Engine That Could. And eventually you got old enough to roam by yourself and discover adventures like the Three Musketeers, Treasure Island and Charlotte’s Web.

But today, all that has changed.

Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, the president of the American Library Association (ALA) says libraries should be used to address ‘systemic racism’ and elevate ‘BIPOC and GLBTQR+ writers and voices.’

Radical librarians call Adventures of Huckleberry Finn and To Kill a Mockingbird “racist.” They’ve stripped Laura Ingalls Wilder’s name from a prestigious book award because of her “problematic’ Little House series.

And they bring in men wearing full makeup, dresses, and high heels for “Drag Queen Story Hours” where books like these are read to children of all ages...

A is for Activist. An ABCboardbook for “families who want their kids to grow up in a space that is unapologetic about activism, environmental justice, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, and everything else that activists believe in and fight for.”

Woke Baby. “For all the littlest progressives, waking up to seize a new day of justice and activism. Woke babies raise their fists in the air. Woke babies cry out for justice. Woke babies grow up to change the world.”

Prince and Knight. The “premier queer-friendly fairy tale” about a prince who marries a knight instead of a princess.

And The Hips on the Drag Queens Go Swish, Swish, Swish. A “family-friendly celebration of drag” that encourages children to “work it.”

I wish I could tell you this was only happening in places like New York City and San Francisco...

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjB9AAwAAAAAAi9Ul8vR5m1-ShMJvfaz1ODFBoqIZy3WdDH-YivZ3XbH79Mgbthr0Jq-7GW6tDVg9qrCykgtYuPm48aLFdw5V1KwYqnWTBJ0ngsP5hFATw

...but that’s just not true.

<- THIS IS A MAN leading “Drag Queen Story Hour.”

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjB9AAwAAAAAAi9Ul8vS97-qGKnuljxWXt1iyya718LZOcFEkhKv9-UC76ZUj6skFLE_Qvri38DHA89iA3r4R_YdYdX04j0aGUP504hIOKw5i_h0BOZiig
That’s why parents and grandparents across the country are rising up through See You At The Library Day.

For decades, the ultra-liberal Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and George Soros’ Open Society have spent millions radicalizing the ALA.

And as a result, a new generation of pink-haired, activist librarians have made it their mission to fill library shelves with anti-American, LGBTQ-friendly, and explicitly sexual content.

Maybe you’ve noticed all the displays at your own library celebrating Pride Month or elevating ‘the environment’ to a type of religion.

Or maybe you’ve noticed the “Teen Zone” which is really meant to be a “parent-free” zone.

The “Teen Zone” is filled with books like: Rick about a cross-dressing Grandpa, Melissa filled with graphic nudity, and Darkstalker featuring gory violence and domestic abuse.

But here’s what’s really alarming.

We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t check out those inappropriate books.”

That may be good for your family -- for now.

But meanwhile, the ALA uses our taxpayer-funded libraries to lure in millions of other children who grow up to be the very activists who are destroying our country and conservative values!

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjB9AAwAAAAAAi9Ul8vTRUBW_5dIp9SWy3778tnqC-DJH2_OjPxGXPFcpP2AETdz8o0NBn--xsVwJl1VdrP5NYGymF1pLQxEvb9YLZtgXuo8SJf9j0LXtQ
I hope you see why I need your help today.

My name is Kirk Cameron.

Maybe you recognize me from the 1980’s family sitcom “Growing Pains” or from my work in inspirational movies like “Fireproof” and “Left Behind.”

I know firsthand how dangerous it is to be indoctrinated by leftist values. Pride almost took me down as a young actor in Hollywood.

But the gospel saved me.

I love being an actor, but what’s far more important is being a husband, dad, grandad, and a Christian.

When I saw what book publishers and libraries were doing to indoctrinate children with anti-God, anti-family, anti-America messages, I knew I had a duty to take action.

So, I wrote a little book called “As You Grow” to teach children how to grow in wisdom through the fruit of the spirit.

Then I decided to go one step further and counter those awful “Drag Queen Story Hours” with conservative Story Hours filled with the classic books you and I grew up with, plus new wholesome books like mine that captivate children with lessons in bravery, honesty, kindness, and patriotism.

And boy, the ALA and radical librarians didn’t like that one

bit.

>> Over 50 libraries rejected my request to host our Story Hour.

>> The ALA helped local libraries scheme ways to keep me out including booking all the event rooms for themselves.

>> Social media blew up with attacks: I was compared to a Nazi (that’s original), my publisher was accused of trying to “confuse and demoralize children,” supporters were described as “bored moms/busybodies who need something to feel good about,” and on and on.

I can’t even print most things these radicals said because it’s so vile.

In the end I got two libraries to reverse course by reminding them that their censorship violated the Constitution of the United States.

And thousands of parents and grandparents brought their little ones to those “Story Hours” where we pledged allegiance to the flag, sang “God Bless America”, and read wholesome and Godly books.

It was incredible.

But here’s the greatest part...

From there, parents and grandparents started asking how they could host “Story Hours” of their own.

And that’s how the nationwide “See You at the Library” movement was born.

Last year, committed conservatives just like you booked event rooms at 201 libraries in 46 states.

On the same day, across America hundreds of “Story Hours”

filled children’s hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God.

Conservative parents, grandparents, and patriots stood together for a very simple mission -- to reject the Left’s radical ideas and reclaim childhood innocence in America’s libraries.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjB9AAwAAAAAAi9Ul8vUjVXJx5Tpg6_RXf1HtaDAvu-9srS9MoV5Zc48EeOPSI5R9EPFWRqH30e8-uFfbxakMXgyXwwUM1n2ZMlGO03JYJNpaGJmE9kaDA
And this year, honoring America’s 250th birthday, my ambitious goal is to expand “See You at the Library Day” to reach 250,000 children.

The exact date will soon be announced. And before then, I need you!

The response from parents, grandparents, and patriots who want to host “Story Hours” has been overwhelming.

That’s a very good thing.

But it’s going to be a big undertaking and expensive to give these volunteers the resources they need to hold “Story Hours” for 250,000 children.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjB9AAwAAAAAAi9Ul8vVsczYEFimfXniGoccs_mJPJGS_QoXSgKQh5YFcj73MKUIhFpr_m6MMVKi0KAZ9e_S5WvalDlTLNjUjhwWLKV7Wtf0UchTcjjnuw
That’s why I’ve teamed with a very special non-profit called BRAVE for Good to make this year’s “See You at the Library Day” a bigger success than ever.

BRAVE for Good was started by BRAVE Books -- the small Christian publisher of my book “As You Grow” –- because so many patriots were asking how they could help “See You at the Library Day” with a tax-deductible gift.

Your sponsorship gift helps send a ‘Story Hour Kit’ to every parent, grandparent, and patriot who’s organizing a “See You at the Library” event.

The kit includes everything they need to bring your conservative values back into our public libraries: instructions for booking their library space and running their Story Hour, small American flags for little ones, fun stickers, wholesome books, Bible memory verse cards, and other specialty items.

Your sponsorship gift is the only way we can fund our “Story Hours” for 250,000 children to counter the radical leftists who’ve taken control of our libraries.

We don’t have the millions behind us like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA.

* * *
# Iran
* **Iran-Oman deal on Hormuz "on verge of being finalized," deputy FM says: **A deal on the Strait of Hormuz between Oman and Iran is "on the verge of being finalized," Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi [told](https://substack.com/redirect/1a5aa52e-67b6-4796-9c53-e3f26f80fdd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran's IRNA news agency on Thursday, saying that the two countries had come to an agreement on nearly all issues, including the location of entry and exit routes for maritime traffic.
* Gharibabadi said that the "new model" for managing traffic through the Strait would have large parts of the shipping route going through Iran's territorial waters, and a smaller portion passing through Omani territorial waters.
* Existing temporary routes, including one near Iran's Larak Island and another southern route near Oman, would be closed.
* **Iran condemns U.S. "breach of promises," claims U.S. ready to return to MOU commitments: **Gharibabadi also discussed Iran's view of the U.S. on Thursday, saying that Iran distrusts the U.S. after its "breach of promises and commitments" under the Islamabad memorandum of understanding.
* The deputy foreign minister [said](https://substack.com/redirect/8fc7e307-17b9-4ab2-959e-976e8d2cd668?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that a return by the U.S. to its obligations under the MOU would be a necessary condition for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but not a sufficient one.
* He [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/933e26ef-53e8-4fa4-a9a4-de53f715567d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Iran had received messages that the U.S. was "fully prepared to return to its commitments" under the June memorandum, including the immediate cessation of military operations.
* **Trump, Vance talk Iran negotiations:** U.S**.** President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance publicly addressed the state of negotiations with Iran on Thursday.
* Speaking in Las Vegas, Trump said he'd "rather make a deal with Iran," because he doesn't "want to kill people." In the same remarks, he repeated an earlier claim that the U.S. was preparing to launch "the biggest attack since World War II" before Iranian officials asked for negotiations.
* Trump also rejected reports of diminishing U.S. stockpiles in a Truth Social [post](https://substack.com/redirect/f1ad0235-e9ec-45d7-bf38-8f9e6e42c683?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday, saying that the Pentagon possessed "massive amounts of 'munitions,' especially of certain types," and that more were being manufactured "as needed." He said that those "leakers" who had claimed otherwise were being "hunted down" and that "long term jail sentences" would be pursued against them.
* Trump [confronted](https://substack.com/redirect/e66e2869-e15d-4a0f-8e9b-0820dc0770cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) War Secretary Pete Hegseth during a Cabinet meeting at Camp David last week demanding to know why he had apparently been misled about severe U.S. munitions shortages, according to the Washington Post. Trump reportedly said he believed the issue "had been fixed." The shortages, particularly of long-range guided missiles and air-defense interceptors, have been one reason Trump has held back from authorizing additional large-scale strikes on Iran in recent days, one source told the outlet.
* Vance, interviewed by Laura Ingraham on Fox News, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/c6e12f90-cdf7-450a-ae25-af3707b9453c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) diplomatic negotiations with Iran were "going to be messy" and would "take some time."
* He also called his Iranian counterparts "extraordinarily difficult people" and blamed the failures on Iran's "fractured system," divided between moderates and hardliners who, he claimed, had pushed the country back into war.
* Vance told Ingraham that he was happy to "own" the negotiating effort, and played down reports that his recent meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had turned hostile. "He didn't confront me. We had a nice and frank conversation," Vance said of the talks.
* **U.S. redirects 48 vessels as part of Iran blockade:** The U.S. military [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/0425ecaf-d06f-451a-b2c4-9866e5f4f483?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday that it had redirected 48 commercial vessels while enforcing its naval blockade of Iran, disabling two and boarding two.
* The statement from CENTCOM also claimed that the U.S. Navy had assisted in more than 1,000 transits over the course of the last three months.
* The maritime tracking firm Kpler [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/cd1ec3bd-2b27-4578-89bc-2e1e97aec4d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday that maritime risk remained "elevated" around the Strait of Hormuz.
* Only two vessels transited the Strait on Wednesday, down from eight the previous day, according to Kpler.

* **Pakistan PM headed to Saudi Arabia:** Pakistan's Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif is scheduled to visit Saudi Arabia on Thursday to discuss consolidating Pakistan-Saudi Arabia bilateral relations and exchange views on developments in the region with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
* The Pakistani delegation includes the country's deputy prime minister/foreign minister, the chief of army staff, the chief of defence forces, as well as other ministers.
* Regarding the U.S. war on Iran, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Tahir Andrabi told a weekly press briefing that Pakistan was "still engaging with other countries" and that it was aiming its diplomatic efforts at "a comprehensive and sustainable solution regarding the Strait of Hormuz."
* **Iran arrests 21 for allegedly spying on its military:** Iran's Ministry of Intelligence announced on Thursday that it had arrested 21 people in the southeastern Kerman Province accused of providing military intelligence to the Israeli spy agency Mossad, according to state broadcaster IRIB.
* **U.S. removes sanctions on Iraqi airline:** The U.S. lifted "counterterrorism" sanctions on at least one airline and several aircraft it previously accused of having ties to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), according to details posted to the U.S. Treasury Department's website on Thursday.
* One of these airlines is Fly Baghdad, according to the website.

This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Iran-Oman deal on Hormuz "on verge of being finalized," deputy FM says: A deal on the Strait of Hormuz between Oman and Iran is "on the verge of being finalized," Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi Iran's IRNA news agency on Thursday, saying that the two countries had come to an agreement on nearly all issues, including the location of entry and exit routes for maritime traffic. Gharibabadi said that the "new model" for managing traffic through the Strait would have large parts of the shipping route going through Iran's territorial waters, and a smaller portion passing through Omani territorial waters. Existing temporary routes, including one near Iran's Larak Island and another southern route near Oman, would be closed. Iran condemns U.S. "breach of promises," claims U.S. ready to return to MOU commitments: Gharibabadi also discussed Iran's view of the U.S. on Thursday, saying that Iran distrusts the U.S. after its "breach of promises and commitments" under the Islamabad memorandum of understanding. The deputy foreign minister that a return by the U.S. to its obligations under the MOU would be a necessary condition for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but not a sufficient one. He that Iran had received messages that the U.S. was "fully prepared to return to its commitments" under the June memorandum, including the immediate cessation of military operations. Trump, Vance talk Iran negotiations: U.S. President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance publicly addressed the state of negotiations with Iran on Thursday. Speaking in Las Vegas, Trump said he'd "rather make a deal with Iran," because he doesn't "want to kill people." In the same remarks, he repeated an earlier claim that the U.S. was preparing to launch "the biggest attack since World War II" before Iranian officials asked for negotiations. Trump also rejected reports of diminishing U.S. stockpiles in a Truth Social on Thursday, saying that the Pentagon possessed "massive amounts of 'munitions,' especially of certain types," and that more were being manufactured "as needed." He said that those "leakers" who had claimed otherwise were being "hunted down" and that "long term jail sentences" would be pursued against them. Trump War Secretary Pete Hegseth during a Cabinet meeting at Camp David last week demanding to know why he had apparently been misled about severe U.S. munitions shortages, according to the Washington Post. Trump reportedly said he believed the issue "had been fixed." The shortages, particularly of long-range guided missiles and air-defense interceptors, have been one reason Trump has held back from authorizing additional large-scale strikes on Iran in recent days, one source told the outlet. Vance, interviewed by Laura Ingraham on Fox News, diplomatic negotiations with Iran were "going to be messy" and would "take some time." He also called his Iranian counterparts "extraordinarily difficult people" and blamed the failures on Iran's "fractured system," divided between moderates and hardliners who, he claimed, had pushed the country back into war. Vance told Ingraham that he was happy to "own" the negotiating effort, and played down reports that his recent meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had turned hostile. "He didn't confront me. We had a nice and frank conversation," Vance said of the talks. U.S. redirects 48 vessels as part of Iran blockade: The U.S. military on Wednesday that it had redirected 48 commercial vessels while enforcing its naval blockade of Iran, disabling two and boarding two. The statement from CENTCOM also claimed that the U.S. Navy had assisted in more than 1,000 transits over the course of the last three months. The maritime tracking firm Kpler on Wednesday that maritime risk remained "elevated" around the Strait of Hormuz. Only two vessels transited the Strait on Wednesday, down from eight the previous day, according to Kpler. Pakistan PM headed to Saudi Arabia: Pakistan's Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif is scheduled to visit Saudi Arabia on Thursday to discuss consolidating Pakistan-Saudi Arabia bilateral relations and exchange views on developments in the region with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The Pakistani delegation includes the country's deputy prime minister/foreign minister, the chief of army staff, the chief of defence forces, as well as other ministers. Regarding the U.S. war on Iran, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Tahir Andrabi told a weekly press briefing that Pakistan was "still engaging with other countries" and that it was aiming its diplomatic efforts at "a comprehensive and sustainable solution regarding the Strait of Hormuz." Iran arrests 21 for allegedly spying on its military: Iran's Ministry of Intelligence announced on Thursday that it had arrested 21 people in the southeastern Kerman Province accused of providing military intelligence to the Israeli spy agency Mossad, according to state broadcaster IRIB. U.S. removes sanctions on Iraqi airline: The U.S. lifted "counterterrorism" sanctions on at least one airline and several aircraft it previously accused of having ties to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), according to details posted to the U.S. Treasury Department's website on Thursday. One of these airlines is Fly Baghdad, according to the website. The U.S. also removed sanctions on two Iraqi individuals on Thursday, whom it accused of close ties to the IRGC, or the previously sanctioned airline. Yemen Ansarallah announces "wide military operation" amid missile and drone attacks on Saudi-backed forces: Several casualties were reported after suspected Ansarallah missile and drone attacks targeted camps belonging to Yemen's Saudi-backed government Emergency Forces in the Marib and Hadramout governorates on Thursday. Local media reported that ballistic missiles and explosive-laden drones struck military camps in Marib and Hadramout, causing multiple casualties. The Emergency Forces said the attacks resulted in "human and material losses" but did not release an official casualty toll. Separately, forces said they shot down an Ansarallah drone over the city of Marib after it entered the city's airspace. An Ansarallah spokesperson said the group would soon announce details of a "wide and qualitative military operation," but did not specify whether he was referring to the reported attacks. Ansarallah claims two strikes on Saudi tankers: Ansarallah military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed on Wednesday that the group had conducted two strikes on Saudi oil tankers over the course of the previous 24 hours, and that it was continuing to enforce its blockade of the kingdom's shipping on both the "south and north of the Red Sea." Saree said the group struck the Saudi oil tanker Daisy in the Gulf of Aden with a ballistic missile, damaging it and forcing it to turn back. The attack followed a similar one on Tuesday on the Saudi oil tanker Wafa. Saree also vowed that the group would let no Saudi tanker pass until "our people's legitimate demands are met, and the siege on them is lifted." Oil spill from suspected Russian shadow fleet tanker threatens Oman 's coast: An alleged Russian shadow fleet tanker stranded off Oman's southern coast is oil across an estimated 600 square kilometers, raising the risk of a major environmental disaster, according to AFP. Satellite imagery reviewed by AFP showed an expanding oil slick near al-Qibliyyah Island, with Greenpeace warning the impact could be "severe and long-lasting." The Caroline Bezengi, which Kpler data indicates loaded one million barrels of Russian crude in May, has been adrift since explosions near Yemen on June 6 disabled its engine and steering, according to maritime security firm Vanguard Tech. The cause of the blasts remains unclear. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, one Palestinian was killed after succumbing to wounds sustained in an earlier attack, and five were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,382 killed, with 174,236 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,255 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,125, while 806 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israel shot sixth-grader in Gaza tent classroom, UN confirms: Israeli forces and wounded a sixth-grade student inside a classroom tent in Gaza City on August 4, the UN confirmed on Wednesday. A day earlier, Israeli forces destroyed the last remaining school in Beit Lahia in what had been a four-school compound. Israel releases 24 Palestinian detainees into Gaza: Israeli authorities 24 Palestinian detainees back into Gaza on Wednesday. They arrived at Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, with at least one carried in on a stretcher, and immediately hospitalized. Israel continues attacks on the occupied West Bank: Qalandia: Israeli forces continued their siege of Qalandia refugee camp and the nearby city of Kafr Aqab for a second day on Thursday, arresting dozens of Palestinians, including a woman with a broken leg after breaking down her door and assaulting her family members, according to WAFA. Soldiers entered dozens of homes in the area, issued demolition threats against businesses, and prevented ambulances from attending to the wounded. Israeli soldiers were also reported to have targeted journalists operating in the area, with one reporter physically assaulted by Israeli soldiers and others facing down stun grenades, according to Al Jazeera. The Palestinian Red Crescent on Thursday that it had treated 16 Palestinians injured by Israelis during the military operation. The Palestinian Prisoner's Society that more than 60 residents of Qalandia were detained and interrogated, including women and children. Israeli soldiers beat detainees during interrogations, used restraints, and threatened detainees with retaliation, according to the group, while vandalizing and seizing property. Nablus: Israeli settlers and injured three Palestinians in Beit Furik, near Nablus, in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday, according to WAFA. Settlers also water in the area on Wednesday, redirecting water pumps used by Palestinians to their settlement outpost. Israeli forces a separate raid on the Askar refugee camp, east of Nablus, on Thursday. Jenin: Israeli soldiers on Thursday to raze land and uproot olive trees in the villages of Zububa and Arabuna, near Jenin, WAFA reported. Hebron: Israeli settlers several homes on fire in the Khirbet Al-Tuba community in the Masafer Yatta area, south of Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday, leaving women and children suffering from smoke inhalation. The Palestine Red Crescent Society said its crews treated six people, including three women, for bruises sustained in the attack. The Israeli military also a home in the village of Birin, near Hebron, on Thursday morning, after raiding the area. Al-Bireh: Israeli soldiers three homes in Al-Bireh on Wednesday evening, storming the neighborhood in which they were located and forcing their inhabitants out at gunpoint. Kfar Qasim: Israeli authorities a home in Kfar Qasim, a Palestinian town in Israel, WAFA reported on Thursday morning. Israeli authorities beat Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya in detention, break his ribs: Israeli authorities severely Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya on July 27, breaking his ribs as part of what the Palestinian Prisoners' Media Office called his "most difficult day." The office reported the doctor, who suffers from heart disease and high blood pressure, has experienced a serious deterioration in his health. Abu Safiya has spent 21 days in solitary confinement during his time in Israeli prison. He has been detained without charge since December 27, 2024, after Israeli forces seized him while he was working as the director of the Kamal Adwan Hospital during attacks on northern Gaza. Arab and Islamic countries condemn Israeli violations in Gaza; Israel army chief says attacks will continue: Arab and Islamic countries including Qatar, Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, Indonesia, Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt a joint statement on Thursday condemning the ongoing Israeli violations in the Gaza Strip, including "the targeting of healthcare facilities and medical infrastructure, attacks on civilian infrastructure, and the continued loss of civilian lives, including women and children." The ministers warned the violations "threaten to derail the political process, reignite the cycle of escalation, and further deepen the humanitarian catastrophe in the Gaza Strip" despite the Palestinian factions' acceptance of the roadmap. Israeli army chief Eyal Zamir in a statement on Thursday that the Israeli military would continue "proactive" operations in Gaza, claiming that the army had "significantly weakened Hamas" and "changed the security reality" in Gaza. Board of Peace awards first building contract in Gaza for military base: The Board of Peace has issued its first construction contract in Gaza to build a rudimentary 150-person military outpost to house Moroccan troops, to the Guardian. The contract, which has not yet been finalized, was awarded to Arkel International, a Louisiana-based company that has previously carried out work with the U.S. government in countries such as Iraq. The base is 100 meters by 120 meters and is intended to house a contingent of Moroccan troops, who would rotate from a base in Israel, the Guardian said, citing a source familiar with the matter. In rare move, Israeli prosecutors charge settler in killing of Palestinian activist Awdah Hathaleen: Israeli prosecutors have filed charges against Yinon Levi, the Israeli settler who shot and killed prominent Palestinian community leader and activist Awdah Hathaleen in the village of Umm al-Khair in the occupied West Bank in July 2025. Levi was charged with reckless manslaughter, which holds a lesser punishment than murder. Other charges include armed trespassing and malicious damage to property. Israeli rights group B'Tselem said that the charges against Levi mark the first time since Oct. 7, 2023, that an Israeli has been indicted for the death of a Palestinian in the West Bank. During that period over 1,100 Palestinians have been killed in attacks by Israeli soldiers and settlers. Read Drop Site 's coverage of the killing of Awdah Hathaleen . Lebanon Israeli attacks wound eight in southern Lebanon as UNIFIL reports 113 projectiles launched: Israeli attacks on the district of Tyre (Sour) in southern Lebanon at least eight people and forced many residents to flee their homes, according to the Lebanese National News Agency, with drone and jet strikes hitting Burj Shemali on Thursday. Additional Israeli strikes hit the towns of Burj Shemali and Al-Mansouri, according to the NNA. Israeli forces also shelled Majdal Zoun, Al-Mansouri, and Haddatha on Thursday morning, and fired at the coastal Al-Hamra area in Bayt Al-Sayyad. UNIFIL Thursday that its peacekeepers continue to observe daily Israeli violations of Lebanese airspace and military activities on the ground, adding that the 113 projectiles launched by the Israeli military on Wednesday were the highest daily total recorded by the mission since June 21. Israeli settlers attempt incursion into Lebanon: A group of about 15 Israeli women affiliated with a settler movement illegally crossed into southern Lebanon on Wednesday, according to The Times of Israel. The Israeli military claimed that it located most of the group and escorted them back into Israel. The women are reportedly part of the Uri Tzafon Movement, a group which seeks to establish Israeli settlements in southern Lebanon. Rights groups condemn Israeli strike that killed Lebanese journalist as a war crime: An Israeli strike which killed Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil and injured photojournalist Zeinab Faraj in southern Lebanon in April amounted to a war crime, , , and said in separate reports on Thursday that all concluded Israeli forces deliberately and directly targeted the two women despite knowing they were civilians. The organizations also found that Israeli forces delayed rescue efforts for hours, dropping stun grenades near Lebanese Red Cross personnel and firing on ambulances, potentially contributing to Khalil's death. They called for a war crimes investigation and accountability, with Human Rights Watch urging states to halt arms sales to Israel and impose targeted sanctions on Israeli officials responsible for ongoing violations. "The impunity enjoyed by Israeli forces for the killing of journalists and other civilians in Lebanon over the past three years has enabled the Israeli military to continue with its unlawful air strikes, including direct attacks on civilians," Amnesty International's Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa, Heba Morayef, said. "It is well past time that the international community impose a comprehensive arms embargo on Israel." At least 15 journalists have been killed by Israel in Lebanon and 210 in Gaza since 2023, according to the UN human rights office. Read Jeremy Loffredo 's report on Khalil's killing for Drop Site . U.S. News Senate committee votes to hold Anthony Fauci in contempt: A Senate committee 8-7 Thursday to hold Anthony Fauci , the former director of the National Institute for Allergy and Infectious Diseases, in contempt of Congress. During a hearing last week before the Government Affairs Committee, chaired by Sen. Rand Paul , Fauci repeatedly invoked his Fifth Amendment right and declined to answer questions. Paul said he would refer the matter to the Justice Department for potential prosecution. Separately, three state attorneys general, led by Florida AG James Uthmeier , announced on Wednesday that they were subpoenaing Fauci over allegations that he "profited" from the recommendations he gave during the Covid-19 pandemic. Fauci, who left government in 2022 and received a preemptive pardon from President Joe Biden , has denied Paul's allegations that he hid information from the public regarding the possible laboratory origins of Covid-19. Sen. Ron Johnson claimed Wednesday that he had obtained a copy of Fauci's government phone and years of his personal diary entries from the Trump administration's Department of Health and Human Services. Trump maintains frequent contact with Fed Chair Warsh, WSJ reports: President Donald Trump has repeatedly with Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh since Warsh took the job less than three months ago, seeking his counsel on issues including the Iran war and artificial intelligence's economic effects, according to a report from The Wall Street Journal. One source cited by the paper said Trump has not raised interest rates directly since Warsh's confirmation. Communication between presidents and Fed chairs has typically been choreographed to avoid the appearance of political influence over rate decisions. Democrats on the Senate Banking Committee have pressed Warsh for more disclosure about his contacts with the president. El-Sayed opposes "unconditional" U.S. military aid to any country, including Israel: Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee in Michigan, outlined his stance in an interview with CNN. "I'm opposed to unconditional military aid for any country. That is Israel, yes, but that's also Egypt, where my family immigrated from. That's Pakistan, that's Saudi Arabia, that's UAE," El-Sayed said. "There are Leahy laws against dealing arms to countries who are engaged in human rights abuses, and I don't want to fund a foreign military that does genocide, apartheid or has taken us to a war we don't need to fight," he added. "I believe in equal rights to peace, dignity, and self-determination for Jewish Israelis and Palestinians alike." Abdul El-Sayed made clear that his opposition to unconditional aid for foreign governments extends to defensive military technology, including Israel's Iron Dome system. "I don't believe that there's really a difference between offensive or defensive weapons, and I also don't believe it's my responsibility to buy defensive weapons for a foreign government when our kids are defenceless against schools that have been underfunded for a very, very long time," he said. Trump-appointed judge ran D.C. PR firm for months after taking bench, ex-employees say: Jennifer Mascott , a Trump-appointed judge on the 3rd Circuit Court of Appeals, deeply involved in operating the Washington public affairs firm Adfero for at least six months after her October 2025 confirmation, according to Politico. Mascott oversaw the firm's staffing, business development, and client relations while working out of its office weekly, according to several former employees and clients. Mascott inherited ownership of the firm from her late husband, Jeff Mascott , in 2023. After taking over the historically nonpartisan firm, she brought on consultants with strong Republican ties, and longtime clients departed, an arrangement sources said drove staff attrition and ultimately led the two-decade-old firm to shut down on June 30. Judicial ethics experts told Politico that Mascott's situation falls into a gray area under rules generally permitting judges to maintain family businesses, though they noted that it could veer into illegality if it interferes with her "judicial duties." USCIS backlog surges to 7.5 million: A work slowdown at the Trump administration's immigration offices has the backlog of citizenship, green card, and work permit applications to an unprecedented 7.5 million people--or more than 12.1 million when including asylum and humanitarian cases--according to the latest agency data cited by Axios. Processing times for naturalization applications have doubled to about 10 months since June 2024, while more than 1.3 million "Dreamers" have waited over six months for work authorization renewals, up from 556,000 two years ago. GAO report finds DOGE overstated federal savings claims: The Government Accountability Office (GAO) that the U.S. Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) Service, the cost-cutting group led by Elon Musk , consistently overstated its claimed savings, taking credit for lease cancellations initiated before the group existed and reporting contracts as terminated when they were not, according to The Washington Post. Of the $110 billion in contract, grant, and lease savings the GAO examined from DOGE's $215 billion "Wall of Receipts"" investigators found more than half of the $61 billion in claimed contract savings was either not actually terminated or could not be corroborated. 108 of 264 leases DOGE listed were already in the process of termination before the group formed, according to the GAO report, which is set for release today. Senate Democrats probe South Korean firm 's $2 million payment to Trump company: Senate Democrats Elizabeth Warren , Richard Blumenthal , and Andy Kim Wednesday that South Korea's Base Group explain a $2 million payment to President Donald Trump's holding company made while the firm's key investment, Korea Aluminium, faced a Commerce Department tariff dispute, writing that the transaction "raises significant concerns about pay-to-play politics and the potential for bribery." "If Base Group were attempting to buy influence with President Trump in an effort to secure lower tariffs or special-interest exemptions for Korea Aluminium, it would be a particularly egregious example of Trump Administration corruption," Sen. Warren wrote. The payment, which the Trump Organization claimed was related to the development of a golf course and which was disclosed in Trump's June financial filing as a "nonrefundable development fee," came shortly before Commerce issued a preliminary finding to impose a 105% tariff on Korea Aluminium's exports. Newly nominated Lawrence pledges to vote for Jeffries for Speaker: Progressive candidate William Lawrence , on Tuesday as the Democratic nominee for Michigan's 7th congressional district, pledged to vote for Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker if elected, reversing a position he held earlier during his campaign. Lawrence, backed by the Democratic Socialists of America, follows Brad Lander , who announced after his election in June that he would vote for Jeffries. Other DSA-backed candidates, including Darializa Avila Chevalier , Melat Kiros , and Chris Rabb , have refused to commit to voting for Jeffries if the Democrats retake the House in November. Lawrence faces a highly contested general election, with his race against Republican Rep. Tom Barrett considered one of the tightest races in the country. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Explosive-laden drone found near Ukrainian cargo plane in Germany : An explosive-equipped drone was at Leipzig Airport near a Ukrainian cargo plane carrying military ammunition, according to local news reports. Forensic investigators reportedly determined that the explosives attached to the drone were military-grade. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt described the incident as a "hybrid attack," although German authorities have not identified those responsible. North Korea fires short-range ballistic missile: North Korea a short-range ballistic missile toward the sea on Thursday, South Korea's military said, the first such launch in more than 40 days. The missile was detected launching from North Korea's Wonsan area around 5 p.m. local time, prompting South Korea's presidential office to hold an emergency security meeting and the country's military to heighten its alert level. Nigerian military rescues 308 kidnapping victims: Nigerian security forces rescued 308 people in separate attacks in the northern Niger and Kwara states, President Bola Tinubu's office announced on Thursday in a major joint rescue operation. More than half, from Kwara's Woro community, had been held since February when gunmen killed at least 170 people. All were freed from the Kainji Lake National Park forest following an operation involving the armed forces, intelligence agency, and police. Flavio Bolsonaro names Congressman Alfredo Gaspar as running mate: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the leading right-wing challenger to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, conservative Congressman Alfredo Gaspar as his running mate. Gaspar, a member of Bolsonaro's Liberal Party who has represented Alagoas in Congress since 2023, led a congressional probe into Brazil's social security institute. Lula's son, Fabio Luis Lula da Silva, is under investigation over allegations he received improper payments linked to pension deductions. UN experts warn of "silent Gaza" in Cuba amid U.S. pressure campaign: United Nations human rights experts on Thursday the U.S.'s ongoing economic and political campaign against Cuba and urged the international community to act quickly to prevent what they called a "silent Gaza" from unfolding on the island. "Food must never be used as an instrument of political pressure," the experts said, adding that measures depriving a population of the means to survive "strike at the most basic guarantees of the rights to life and diminish the core of human dignity." Iraqi government says armed groups could face terrorism charges after deadline: The governing coalition in charge of Iraq issued a statement on Thursday warning that any groups within the country who possessed arms after a deadline of September 30 would be "considered an outlaw" and could face charges under Iraq's anti-terrorism law. Canadian PM defends ICC: Prime Minister Mark Carney reaffirmed Canada's support for the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Thursday, saying Ottawa would continue funding the institution despite U.S. pressure on allies to withdraw support. The Trump administration has waged a public campaign against the ICC after the court issued arrest warrants for Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, over charges related to its genocide in Gaza. And it’s not just groceries. Families are feeling the squeeze everywhere. Housing. Health care. Gas. A grandma told me that even diapers are nearly $50 a week.
People are working hard, but they’re being asked to do more with less because their government isn’t standing up for them.

I’m a former geologist and one of the only published scientists in the U.S. Senate. I also helped open Colorado’s first brewpub, The Wynkoop, in 1988 and began the rejuvenation of downtown Denver. At The Wynkoop, there was no problem we couldn’t solve over a fresh, Colorado beer. Eventually, I found myself in public service. But I didn’t run for office for fame, or money, or power. I ran because I wanted to bring people together and actually make everyday life better for Colorado families. That’s exactly what we’ve done. (I also hated having a boss!) As Denver’s Mayor, we unified the metro area to expand and rejuvenate our public transit. We also initiated the most significant police reforms in Denver’s history, and provided high-quality Early Childhood Education for every four-year-old in the city. As Governor, we took Colorado’s economy from 40th to #1 in the nation for three straight years. And as your Senator, we wrote and passed the largest-ever effort to fight climate change, passed the most consequential housing bill in decades, and brought money and jobs back to our state. Now I’m running for re-election to help Democrats take back the Senate and bring MAGA’s ruthless agenda to a halt. And to finish fixing what we started under President Biden! A few weeks ago, I had the honor of joining my friend Senator Amy Klobuchar at a reproductive rights rally — and I'm still riding the energy from it.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26]
The turnout was incredible. Seeing that many people show up in force to fight for reproductive freedom reminded me exactly why I ran for office in the first place.
Eight years ago, I was just a doctor living in a red district represented by a MAGA extremist. I decided to run because I knew what Trump's promise to appoint anti-choice justices to the Supreme Court with the explicit intent of overturning Roe would mean for my patients, and for people across our country.
We knocked on thousands of doors, had thousands of conversations, and won by 216 votes. That victory belonged to all of us.
Since then, the fight has only gotten more difficult, and the stakes have gotten even higher.
But we’ve also seen what happens when we all come together and make our voices heard. Whenever abortion rights have been on the ballot these last few years, they’ve won. Because people want the right to make decisions about their own bodies and we are not going back.
And the energy I saw at this rally tells me everything I need to know about where we're headed.
We are days away from the primary, and less than three months away from the general election on November 3rd. Flipping the House and electing pro-choice majorities up and down the ballot is how we protect reproductive rights for every Minnesotan and every American.
That work is happening right now — in conversations with friends and family, in volunteering for campaigns like mine, and in chipping in when you can. If you’re able to contribute before the primary, I’d be so grateful for your support. Every dollar goes towards our $15,000 online goal and helps power our ground game in these final days before the general election kicks off:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26]
That's how we won before — and it's how we'll win again.
With gratitude and resolve,
Kelly

clean_body: [] A few weeks ago, I had the honor of joining my friend Senator Amy Klobuchar at a reproductive rights rally — and I'm still riding the energy from it. [] The turnout was incredible. Seeing that many people show up in force to fight for reproductive freedom reminded me exactly why I ran for office in the first place. Eight years ago, I was just a doctor living in a red district represented by a MAGA extremist. I decided to run because I knew what Trump's promise to appoint anti-choice justices to the Supreme Court with the explicit intent of overturning Roe would mean for my patients, and for people across our country. We knocked on thousands of doors, had thousands of conversations, and won by 216 votes. That victory belonged to all of us. Since then, the fight has only gotten more difficult, and the stakes have gotten even higher. But we’ve also seen what happens when we all come together and make our voices heard. Whenever abortion rights have been on the ballot these last few years, they’ve won. Because people want the right to make decisions about their own bodies and we are not going back. And the energy I saw at this rally tells me everything I need to know about where we're headed. We are days away from the primary, and less than three months away from the general election on November 3rd. Flipping the House and electing pro-choice majorities up and down the ballot is how we protect reproductive rights for every Minnesotan and every American. That work is happening right now — in conversations with friends and family, in volunteering for campaigns like mine, and in chipping in when you can. name: Jamie Davis
subject: The farming accident that changed my life
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jamie Davis for U
body:
August 8th, 2008, the worst day of my life, changed how I see everything: from family to the importance of our rural communities and it is a key part of why I am running for office.
| | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018NRAi8YlAkrAJwPgg3R74H3Y4twor4eSjCGlWxmd0k9Ra3XM4A1okvEw-t4qxWkbPJDNXlqWd6EL2Mk8MWzltmxwejpcrNRuP-j_N4P2TIjph-Se-V1TxRS7HwSr6Fagmsa_FlsxlWmW9MaSnAJOyAPLlwX333kMU-7x9h9fd8eSjoDiyuL3D2rY9vyHsnk0PB-jtIZKUiukZ75QHDA64_Hu7Ac5UC_V&c=YJI-dTSZBXFOKuq3P1ErF5ZCMEi-R3g0HTj2dIW1CMMRE3QIqTCNXw==&ch=o8d3_wsBbTFBiXviphiIWxwVpPrzGAaUk02Q8yX2sa9EPyUFs1MaVQ==)
---
| Peter,
August 8, 2009, is a date I will never forget.
Just days before his 19th birthday, my son Justin was out in the fields with us, doing what this family has done for over three generations--farming the Louisiana delta. A breakdown in our combine left corn spilled across the ground, and as we worked to recover it, Justin got too close. In an instant, his pant leg was caught, and the thresher pulled him in.
I can still hear his voice: "Dad, get me out."
And there was nothing I could do.
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018NRAi8YlAkrAJwPgg3R74H3Y4twor4eSjCGlWxmd0k9Ra3XM4A1okvEw-t4qxWkbPJDNXlqWd6EL2Mk8MWzltmxwejpcrNRuP-j_N4P2TIjph-Se-V1TxRS7HwSr6Fagmsa_FlsxlWmW9MaSnAJOyAPLlwX333kMU-7x9h9fd8eSjoDiyuL3D2rY9vyHsnk0PB-jtIZKUivDxVPahsRxszb-8k7KXBSO&c=YJI-dTSZBXFOKuq3P1ErF5ZCMEi-R3g0HTj2dIW1CMMRE3QIqTCNXw==&ch=o8d3_wsBbTFBiXviphiIWxwVpPrzGAaUk02Q8yX2sa9EPyUFs1MaVQ==)
---
My son and I on the farm in 2021.
Multiple miracles occurred that day: When it initially happened he wasn't in pain because his nerves were pinched so tightly in the machine. Nor was he bleeding because he was caught so tight in there.
It took the jaws of life to tear apart that machine and when the metal finally gave way he let out a scream that I will never forget for the rest of my life.
The paramedics quickly sprang into action and he was airlifted to Jackson, Mississippi, where Doctors fought to save his leg, but the injury and infection from all the dirt and debris were too severe. Justin lost his leg from below the knee.
That day could have broken us. Instead, it showed me what makes Louisiana strong.
Neighbors, first responders from two parishes (what we call counties in Louisiana), and a doctor who wasn't even on duty, Dr. Ron Gregg, a farmer himself and longtime family friend -- showed up because that's what rural communities do. They take care of each other. They don't ask if it's their job or jurisdiction. They just show up.
Today, Justin is 35. He runs our farm. He's built a life, with a fiancee and a family of his own. He still hunts, fishes, and works the land -- just with a prosthetic leg and the same determination that carried him through that day.
But the truth is, the kind of community that saved Justin is disappearing. Rural hospitals are closing. Doctors like Dr. Gregg--who live in our communities, who know our families--are harder to find. Too many of our kids feel like they have to leave home to build a future.
And my family, who first worked this Louisiana delta soil as sharecroppers, and now as farmers who own this land, have put too much blood into this soil for us to leave and go somewhere else.
I have to take a stand and fight for our way of life and it's why I am proud to be the Democrat running for Senate in Louisiana.
If you believe in that fight, I'm asking you to stand with me today. A Democratic win here is the first step in taking our state back from the far-right whose policies of atomization and vicious corporatism are tearing our communities apart.
And mark my words, a win is possible, Democrats just won a deep red special election here by a landslide. [The blue wave will wash over Louisiana and we will flip this seat but only if we fight for it. Will you please make a contribution of $25, $10, or even just $5 to help us in our fight to restore the Louisiana that we love so dearly.](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0018NRAi8YlAkrAJwPgg3R74H3Y4twor4eSjCGlWxmd0k9Ra3XM4A1okvEw-t4qxWkb8bDT97aO4uLQxIgs7FbC6wCn-Co7zyj-wHRykcqs_1m_60ZEhYowuDp6Re-By14_qoywROehSE-yp9QyDCVhdAGuCmO2VJSRI0wPH1m1e6JDdX49GLS6GVM90-5zK_1RQSGftBV9AezNJ6qmNcmOUoDaVqZ2tHkHP_5X-oLyZSE=&c=YJI-dTSZBXFOKuq3P1ErF5ZCMEi-R3g0HTj2dIW1CMMRE3QIqTCNXw==&ch=o8d3_wsBbTFBiXviphiIWxwVpPrzGAaUk02Q8yX2sa9EPyUFs1MaVQ==)

clean_body: August 8th, 2008, the worst day of my life, changed how I see everything: from family to the importance of our rural communities and it is a key part of why I am running for office. | | | | | == | Peter, August 8, 2009, is a date I will never forget. Just days before his 19th birthday, my son Justin was out in the fields with us, doing what this family has done for over three generations--farming the Louisiana delta. A breakdown in our combine left corn spilled across the ground, and as we worked to recover it, Justin got too close. In an instant, his pant leg was caught, and the thresher pulled him in. I can still hear his voice: "Dad, get me out." And there was nothing I could do. | == My son and I on the farm in 2021. Multiple miracles occurred that day: When it initially happened he wasn't in pain because his nerves were pinched so tightly in the machine. Nor was he bleeding because he was caught so tight in there. It took the jaws of life to tear apart that machine and when the metal finally gave way he let out a scream that I will never forget for the rest of my life. The paramedics quickly sprang into action and he was airlifted to Jackson, Mississippi, where Doctors fought to save his leg, but the injury and infection from all the dirt and debris were too severe. Justin lost his leg from below the knee. That day could have broken us. Instead, it showed me what makes Louisiana strong. Neighbors, first responders from two parishes (what we call counties in Louisiana), and a doctor who wasn't even on duty, Dr. Ron Gregg, a farmer himself and longtime family friend -- showed up because that's what rural communities do. They take care of each other. They don't ask if it's their job or jurisdiction. They just show up. Today, Justin is 35. He runs our farm. He's built a life, with a fiancee and a family of his own. He still hunts, fishes, and works the land -- just with a prosthetic leg and the same determination that carried him through that day. But the truth is, the kind of community that saved Justin is disappearing. Rural hospitals are closing. Doctors like Dr. Gregg--who live in our communities, who know our families--are harder to find. Too many of our kids feel like they have to leave home to build a future. And my family, who first worked this Louisiana delta soil as sharecroppers, and now as farmers who own this land, have put too much blood into this soil for us to leave and go somewhere else. I have to take a stand and fight for our way of life and it's why I am proud to be the Democrat running for Senate in Louisiana. If you believe in that fight, I'm asking you to stand with me today. A Democratic win here is the first step in taking our state back from the far-right whose policies of atomization and vicious corporatism are tearing our communities apart. Join Anthony DiLorenzo and Congressman Bryan Steil, Chairman of the U.S. House Committee on House Administration, for an important conversation about the future of American elections.
As Chairman, Congressman Steil is leading congressional efforts to strengthen election integrity and advance commonsense reforms, including proof-of-citizenship and voter-identification requirements.
Come learn more about the SAVE Act and the work being done to protect our elections, restore public confidence, and ensure American elections are for Americans.

clean_body: | | | Across the Commonwealth | VIRGINIA SALES TAX HOLIDAY -Aug. 7-9 Virginia's three day sales tax holiday is this weekend! The 3-day sales tax holiday starts August 7th at 12:01 am and ends on August 9th at 11:59 pm. During the sales tax holiday, you can buy qualifying school supplies, clothing, footwear, and hurricane and emergency preparedness items without paying sales tax. | ~ | VIRGINIA HOUSE OF DELEGATES PAGE PROGRAM APPLICATIONS OPEN Each year, the Speaker of the House of Delegates appoints 13- and 14-year-olds from across the Commonwealth to work in the House Clerk's Office as House Pages during the Regular Session of the Virginia General Assembly. They assist the Delegates and staff in the House Clerk's Office in performing a wide variety of daily duties required for the successful operation of the House. Applications are open now through October 16. | In the Community | | SALEM VA SUMMER VETFEST ENROLLMENT FAIR On Saturday, August 29, the Salem VA Medical Center will host a Summer VetFest Enrollment Fair from 11am-2pm. This event is a one-stop-shop to connect Veterans to VA Health Care, benefits, and Salem VA Health Care System programs and resources. Many VA services will be offered on the spot including enrollment in VA Health Care and same-day appointments with a VA doctor. ~ | ROANOKE NATIONAL NIGHT OUT 2026 Our city knows how to have a good time. National Night Out was another successful night of community here in the Star City! With events all over the city hosted by neighborhood associations, and a central city event at Eureka Recreational Center, this night was a blast filled with music, games, and a good time. | POEMS & COFFEE: SCHOOL SUPPLIES DRIVE - Aug. 6 Bring your blankets and your picnics and don't miss this special edition of Poems & Coffee! There will be an open mic and artist features for all to vibe out to before the kids head back to school at Fishburn Mansion. All are welcome to bring school supplies to fill up backpacks that will be donated to Roanoke City Public Schools. ~~ | COMMONWEALTH DAY OF PLAY \- Aug. 8 The Commonwealth Day of Play is returning to Roanoke! Don't miss it on Saturday, Aug. 8 with free outdoor activities for children and families from noon to 4pm at Brookside Par 3 Golf Course, 3704 Carvins Cove Rd. City Council issued a proclamation declaring Aug. 8, 2026, as Commonwealth Day of Play in the City of Roanoke, and a member of the Governor's team will be attending this wonderful event! | BIG LICK COMIC CON - Aug. 8-9 Get ready, Roanoke! Big Lick Comic Con is bringing its unique blend of comic culture, entertainment, and positivity! It will be two unforgettable days filled with incredible exhibitors, guests, artists, cosplay, gaming, vendors, and more. Whether you're a hardcore comic book fan, a movie buff, or just looking for family-friendly entertainment, there's something for everyone at this exciting new celebration. | TOUCH-A-TRUCK \- Aug. 8 Touch-A-Truck revs up again for the 15th anniversary at Roanoke County's Green Hill Park this August! Explore, interact, and learn about dozens of fascinating vehicles. Step inside, climb aboard, and engage with the operators. name: Ken Burns
subject: Roy Cooper
body:
Winning this race is absolutely critical if we’re going to flip the Senate.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1009&source=&t=1&akid=2521%2E124072%2E3H4F7X)
| | | |
---
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1009&amount=5&t=8&akid=2521%2E124072%2E3H4F7X)
Hi, Peter – it’s Ken Burns.
Today, I’m asking you to make a donation to Roy Cooper’s campaign for U.S. Senate in North Carolina. Winning this race is absolutely critical if we’re going to flip the Senate, so I hope you’ll join me in supporting Roy. [**_Will you chip in $5?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1009&amount=5&t=9&akid=2521%2E124072%2E3H4F7X)
Across this country, people are hurting in ways that don’t always make the history books but shape lives all the same.
The grocery bills that are too high. A lifesaving prescription that forces a difficult choice. A paycheck that just doesn’t stretch as far as it once did. | These are the real pressures that define a moment.
**Roy Cooper has spent much of his life as a public servant working to ease those burdens.**
Not seeking attention but doing the work. Expanding access to affordable health care. Investing in public schools. Defending the idea that government, at its best, is not distant – but present, steady and accountable to the people it serves.
It is the kind of leadership that rarely makes noise, but over time, it leaves a mark.
Right now, there are those who want to take North Carolina – and our country – in a different direction. They see division as a strategy; they mistake power for purpose. They are organized. They are well-funded by dark-money and special interest groups.
**The only way we can defeat them is if dedicated, caring people like you choose not to sit back but to take part. The power rests in our hands, and we must use it.**
[**_Will you make a donation of $5 or any amount today to help Roy flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1009&amount=5&t=10&akid=2521%2E124072%2E3H4F7X)
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14275?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1009&amount=5&t=11&akid=2521%2E124072%2E3H4F7X)
---
| | [DONATE $25](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14275?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1009&amount=25&t=12&akid=2521%2E124072%2E3H4F7X)

---

---
Help ensure that the next chapter of North Carolina reflects the very best of what this state has always tried to be.
Thank you for doing your part,

Ken Burns
| |
* * *
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1009&t=2&akid=2521%2E124072%2E3H4F7X)
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

**_[Donate today to help win this seat and flip the Senate blue.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1009&source=&t=3&akid=2521%2E124072%2E3H4F7X)_**

subject: End dark money influence now
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Bennett for Governor · P
body:
The people of Maine deserve to know exactly who their next Governor will answer to

| | |
---
---
---
---
Peter, **The people of Maine deserve to know exactly whom their next Governor will answer to.** I've been clear from the very beginning. As Governor, I will answer to the people of Maine – and only the people of Maine. Not party insiders. Not dark money special interests. Not corporate lobbyists. The question is: who will my opponents answer to? Right now, Maine voters don't have the information they need to answer that question. That needs to change. **Today, I'm calling for three simple acts of transparency.**
1. **Bobby Charles should disclose his corporate lobbying and consulting clients, how much each paid him, the work he performed on their behalf, and the government action he sought.** After decades of lobbying for and advising powerful interests, Maine voters deserve to know whose interests he has been advancing and whether those relationships would follow him into the Blaine House**.**
2. **Hannah Pingree should call on the dark money organizations supporting her campaign to disclose the donors behind their spending. If they refuse, she should publicly reject their support.** A group affiliated with the Democratic Governors Association has already reserved $11 million in advertising for this race. Maine voters deserve to know who is paying for those ads and what they expect in return.
3. **Both of my opponents should join me in supporting a true donor transparency law that traces political money back to its original source.** If someone is trying to influence a Maine election, Maine voters have a right to know who they are.

Because that's what this is really about. While Maine families are struggling with higher housing costs, higher energy bills, higher health care costs, and a government that too often seems to work better for insiders than for the people, the political establishment is preparing to flood this election with outside money and hidden influence. That is the system I’m running against. **I’m running for the people of Maine.** And, I need your help to do so.
---

This campaign is about giving Maine people their voice back. It's about making sure working families, older Mainers, small business owners, and young people trying to build a future here have a Governor who answers to them – not party bosses, not national political operatives, and not anonymous donors writing million-dollar checks behind closed doors. We're up against powerful interests. But I've never believed elections belong to the biggest checkbook. I believe they belong to the people. If you believe Maine should belong to the people who live here, work here, and raise their families here \- not to the corrupt interests trying to buy influence - then I need you to join us today. **Please chip in now and help us build a campaign strong enough to fight for Maine’s future.**

name: Andrew Sneed for Congress
subject: The Last 6 Weeks and the Next 90 Days!
body:
Since the runoff, we've been working hard! The election is coming up quickly and we need to be ready!
---
| | | | [ View in browser](https://h8g0t.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/mr/sh/SMJz09SDriOHTaoDGkpqIpMfjg9x/zFV6XBtMi25S)
---
| | | | |
---
| | | Peter,
It's been a busy six weeks since we came out of the primary, and we wanted to give you a real look at what our campaign has been building on the ground! If you're tired of the status quo and want to make a change, please reach out. We can win in AL-05 if we work together!
**CANVASSING & PHONEBANKING ARE UNDERWAY**
With only 89 days until Election Day, we're working hard to expand our presence across the district and every voting precinct. We officially launched our general election volunteer operation, and between door knocks and phone calls, our volunteers have already made over 2,000 voter contacts across all 6 counties in the district. Every conversation matters, this district deserves a representative who shows up -- and that starts with us showing up at the door.
---
| [ Join Us & Volunteer!](https://h8g0t.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/SMK1E8tHeFuBlbNaKGvxQIyuMhJZ/73VMu9f131ek)
---
**TOWN HALLS ACROSS THE DISTRICT**
We'll be holding town halls in Scottsboro, Decatur, Athens, and Huntsville to hear directly from the people I hope to represent. I'd love to see you there and hear from you directly.
Doors open at 5:30 PM for each event:August 17, 6:00 PM — Bynum Auditorium, Scottsboro, ALAugust 26, 6:00 PM — Turner Surles Center, Decatur, ALSeptember 9, 6:00 PM — McCandless Hall, Athens, ALOctober 5, 6:00 PM — Bob Harrison Center, Huntsville, AL
|
---
Mark your calendar and come out if you can. This campaign is about listening as much as it is about talking, and that starts with you in the room.
We've invited Representative Strong to participate, but have yet to hear back from his team.
| [ RSVP Online!](https://h8g0t.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/SMK1E8tHeG13DkCXVR5RW8HeKztp/RY0lUocnQ5Yg)
---
**OUTRAISING THE INCUMBENT**
Last quarter, this campaign outraised Dale Strong, funded entirely by people like you. That kind of grassroots support is unheard of in AL-05, and it's proof that this district is ready for a change.
**WHERE WE'RE HEADED**
AL-05 hasn't had a real fight in a long time. We're building the kind of campaign that wins -- funded by people, not PACs, and powered by volunteers who believe Alabama deserves better than what it's gotten.
Thank you for being part of this effort. The math is there, we just have to motivate as many people as possible to get to the polls and vote for change. We can use your help - following along and sharing our posts on social media, knocking doors or making calls, or just by being ready to show up to the polls on election day.
| [ Join Us!](https://h8g0t.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/SMK1E8tHeG7uft1UgbEvbxaOJIU5/51Nw_qbao9cI)
---
|
Thank you for your support! Now, let's get to work!
- Andrew Sneed

---

| | | |
---

614 Madison Street, 35801, Huntsville

## **ICYMI: NH Journal: Uber Conflict: Pappas Backs Bill With Liability Shield for Husband’s Employer**
---
| | | | | |

**Uber Conflict: Pappas Backs Bill With Liability Shield for Husband’s Employer
** Michael Graham
[NH Journal
](https://us.list-manage.com/JPSDNK0yNMZ?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=xWGVmzRnSyYiF7vPpH-sgX4t7znaDxdgianh78ZiUVpql23OC3YIk602Wg==)August 4, 2026 _Democrat Chris Pappas has made ethics and transparency a centerpiece of his U.S. Senate campaign.__...__But at the same time Pappas has been positioning himself as a good-government reformer, he has been involved in a very public ethical conflict that critics call problematic.__Pappas serves on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, which writes the federal rules governing ride-hailing companies such as Uber and Lyft. His husband, Vann Bentley, is a policy executive at Uber.__According to Pappas’ financial disclosures, the couple holds between $150,000 and $350,000 in Uber stock received as part of Bentley’s compensation, along with a smaller stake in Amazon, where Bentley previously lobbied.__**In May, Pappas voted to advance federal legislation that would strip sexual assault victims of the right to sue ride-hailing companies such as Uber and Lyft over harm caused by their drivers. It was part of the BUILD America 250 Act, a sweeping five-year surface transportation bill.**__Under current law, when an Uber driver rapes, gropes, or otherwise harms a passenger, that passenger can sue not only the driver but Uber itself — the company that recruited the driver, ran the background check, and put him on the road.__...__But when the entire bill came before the committee, it passed 62-2 with Pappas’ support.__... Republicans disagree, pointing out that Pappas knew the amendment would pass with or without his vote.__“Chris Pappas voted for the bill to become law. Everything else is just performative,” said Samantha Cantrell of the National Republican Senatorial Committee._ Read more [here](https://us.list-manage.com/JgP_oOzwfl0?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=m4Fktaqzs4Ie8kkVIlNJNjvPVcyHWQ4Qw4PlceeOECHdqDVaxKw1PKeMJQ==).

clean_body: We're working together to elect Democrats up and down the ballot. | Team, I want to congratulate Jocelyn Benson, Abdul El-Sayed, and every Democrat who won up and down the ballot in Michigan's primary election on Tuesday. They have my support as we come together to fight like hell and win in November. The MAGA Republican agenda has driven up costs for families here in Michigan and across the country. We know John James, Mike Rogers, and the rest of the Republican ticket would be rubber stamps for Donald Trump’s agenda, including the failed tariff policies that have raised the cost of gas, groceries, and everyday essentials. Michigan Democrats are offering a different path. We’re fighting to lower costs, build more affordable housing, make health care more accessible, and deliver real results for working families. There was a lot of passion and energy throughout these primaries, and that’s a good thing. Now, Democrats across the state are united by a shared goal: getting things done for the people of Michigan. There is so much on the line this November, from health care costs to our fundamental freedoms. The truth is, Texas is the last bastion of liberty and the lone bulwark against Democrat tyranny.

As I continue to travel across the state, I hope I get the chance to meet you, shake your hand, and thank you for being a patriot.

name: Jenny Beth Martin, Tea Party Patriots Action
subject: No vacation until voter ID passes
body:
Photo identification to vote is sitting in the Senate. Recess starts next week.
[](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org/1/0100019fd81a5a0d-7354f821-8dfd-4125-8a1d-03453dfbb3a4-000000/bvA1ca0iPxuxYQsTUe8k8fLhc595iW4BGnJZ7S9HcpY=452)Patriot–The United States Senate is scheduled to leave Washington for its August recess next week.Sitting on the calendar, already passed by the House of Representatives, is H.R. 7008, the Stop Insider Trading Act.That bill does two things.It bars members of Congress, their spouses, and their dependent children from buying individual stocks while they hold office.And it writes photo identification to vote into federal law.Read that second one again. Voter ID. The reform you and I have been fighting for, for years. It cleared the House of Representatives on July 22 by a vote of 232 to 198, and thirteen Democrats crossed over to vote for it.Now it needs sixty votes in the Senate. And the Senate would rather go on vacation.I am asking you for one more push before they leave.**Here is what I need you to do today:** 1\. **Call the Capitol switchboard at 202-224-3121.** Ask to be connected to your United States Senator. Then call back and ask for your other Senator. Both offices need to hear from you.2\. **Tell each office exactly this:**
> _"Do not leave Washington for the August recess until the Senate passes the Stop Insider Trading Act, H.R. 7008, and puts voter identification into federal law."_
3\. [_**Add your name to the petition.**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Faction.teapartypatriots.org%2Fpetition%2Fnovacation%2F/1/0100019fd81a5a0d-7354f821-8dfd-4125-8a1d-03453dfbb3a4-000000/6b3fF17syARNe_KfTFVL-9UE5FX4rA74oECTuOAIRVs=452) It goes to the Senate Majority Leader with your name on it.[TELL THE SENATE: NO VACATION](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Faction.teapartypatriots.org%2Fpetition%2Fnovacation%2F/2/0100019fd81a5a0d-7354f821-8dfd-4125-8a1d-03453dfbb3a4-000000/FH-Grwg466q9mO52nF2ut8pkL9ml_gTZ0cLO4tWxPiM=452)Now let me be straight with you about what this bill is and is not.H.R. 7008 is not the SAVE America Act. It does not require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote. We are still fighting for that, and I am not letting it go.But voter identification is in this bill. It has already passed the House of Representatives. And it is the one piece of election integrity sitting on the Senate calendar today, with a deadline attached to it.At least fourteen senators have already said publicly that they will not go quietly into recess with this undone. Senator Mike Lee has committed to forcing a roll call vote on adjournment, so every senator has to go on the record about whether election integrity or a summer break comes first.That is what pressure looks like when it is working. Your phone call is what keeps it building.There is no version of this where the Senate serves the country by going home early.One call today. Both offices. Ninety seconds.In liberty,Jenny Beth Martin
Chairman, Tea Party Patriots Action******P.S. Forward this to one person who will pick up the phone today.** The Senate is counting on August being the month nobody is paying attention. Let us prove otherwise. name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: We’re down ONE POINT
body:
Taking back Texas this year is in our sights.
#
Friend —
I need you to sit with this number for a second: **one point.**
That's it. That's the entire gap between me and Greg Abbott right now, according to a brand-new Fox News poll — yes, Fox News.
[](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21583?c0=leftnet_em20260806_partner_ms_gh_em_leftnet.9jZSV2&refcode=em20260806-1702&t=1&akid=1702%2E2118727%2Elcjudl)
In nearly twelve years as governor, through three elections, Greg Abbott has never faced a poll this close. Not once. His campaign has already spent over $54 million this cycle just to hang on to power. This poll says people aren’t buying what he’s selling anymore.
Here's why it's happening: Texans are falling behind financially and they know exactly who's been in charge while it happened. Nearly 4 in 10 Texans say inflation is the top issue on their minds — **and after 12 years of Greg Abbott, they're done waiting around for things to get better.**
I'm not surprised. I've been hearing it at every stop — from Brownsville to Austin to Amarillo. Families are tired of watching their grocery bills and insurance premiums climb while Abbott hands billions to his donors.
**This 1-point poll shows that a new chapter for Texas is finally in reach.** But it’s not guaranteed. Turnout will decide this election. And Abbott's team knows it — they're going to spend the next 89 days doing everything they can to make sure Texans who are ready for change don't show up to the polls to vote. They will do anything to keep Texans from turning the page on his failed administration.
I can't outspend Greg Abbott, and I don’t need to. Our campaign can out-organize him, but that takes people like you stepping up right now to raise the resources we need to win this race.
**[Can you chip in $15 to my campaign to help us keep closing this gap and — finally — take back Texas?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22962?c0=leftnet_em20260806_partner_ms_gh_em_leftnet.xm6ShT&refcode=em20260806-1702&t=2&akid=1702%2E2118727%2Elcjudl)**
**[DONATE ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21583?c0=leftnet_em20260806_partner_ms_gh_em_leftnet.9jZSV2&refcode=em20260806-1702&t=3&akid=1702%2E2118727%2Elcjudl)**
We've never been this close. Let's make sure we don't waste this opportunity.
Gina
