# [High leverage warning from Jamie Dimon has real teeth](https://substack.com/redirect/c24cc461-3c1c-49c8-b2a1-db191914d599?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon warned that leverage across financial markets remains elevated, with margin debt the highest it has ever been, **[raising chances somebody will disrupt the market quickly.](https://substack.com/redirect/5b877957-e153-4aa6-8a4c-c065821f0312?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c24cc461-3c1c-49c8-b2a1-db191914d599?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Highest margin debt ever:** Dimon said margin debt is the highest it has ever been, with much hidden under other names through prime brokerages, hedge funds, ETFs and Treasury arbitrage strategies.
* **Quick disruption chance:** Heavy leverage creates a higher chance that somebody will disrupt the market in a quick way and people get rattled over it, he told CNBC.
* **Isolated failures absorbed:** The recent heavy losses at AI hedge fund Situational Awareness, where JPMorgan was a prime broker, showed markets can absorb such episodes without broader disruption.
* **Not called systemic:** Dimon stopped short of labeling the high leverage systemic, noting actual losses matter more than leverage alone, as seen with mortgages in 2008.

# [SpaceX stock cut in half but the buying doesn't stop](https://substack.com/redirect/8a042787-9814-4357-8452-b4d72958d5bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
SpaceX shares closed at 108.27 after a 13.61% drop, **[more than half off the June peak,](https://substack.com/redirect/b293e2b7-b2a4-4f1e-8958-f79c367f4b61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** yet retail investors bought every day since the IPO while ARK Invest added $14.5 million dollars in shares.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8a042787-9814-4357-8452-b4d72958d5bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Retail buying never stops:** **[Investors net purchased $22.7 million dollars of SpaceX in Wednesday's first hour,](https://substack.com/redirect/b293e2b7-b2a4-4f1e-8958-f79c367f4b61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** more than three times the average and the third-largest haul across 37 sessions since the IPO.
* **ARK Invest buys SpaceX:** Cathie Wood's firm **[acquired 128,932 SpaceX shares valued at roughly $14.5 million dollars](https://substack.com/redirect/39cf8c6b-3aef-466c-9934-84b079230dba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after the decline as part of a $28.7 million dollar combined investment with TSMC.
* **Earnings reveal AI costs:** First public results topped revenue and adjusted earnings expectations, yet nearly $16 billion dollars in quarterly AI and data center spending contributed to the sharp stock selloff.
* **Lockup expires this Thursday:** Up to 912 million shares from employees and pre-IPO investors become eligible for sale, potentially more than doubling the public float without requiring any actual sales.

# [Lilly pulls further ahead in GLP-1 race as Novo doubts mount](https://substack.com/redirect/8a042787-9814-4357-8452-b4d72958d5bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Both Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk beat second-quarter estimates and raised full-year outlooks, **[yet investors cheered Lilly's results while punishing Novo,](https://substack.com/redirect/8e6c69f6-4c01-4853-949e-add5492cd230?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** underscoring a growing divide between the obesity drug giants.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8a042787-9814-4357-8452-b4d72958d5bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Lilly market share lead:** Lilly held a 60.9% share of the U.S. obesity and diabetes drug market in the second quarter compared with Novo Nordisk's 38.8%, according to its earnings presentation.
* **Lilly revenue surge:** Resilient demand for Mounjaro and Zepbound pushed Lilly revenue up 48% from a year ago as the company hiked its full-year revenue guidance despite lower U.S. prices.
* **Novo pill shortfall:** Revenue of Novo's Wegovy pill came in slightly below analyst estimates even after reaching more than 5 million patients since its January U.S. launch.
* **Pipeline setbacks noted:** Novo reported mixed CagriSema results that failed to match Zepbound on blood sugar control, plus a recent heart drug that failed to reduce major cardiovascular events.

# [New Ford EV pickup shocks with $28,350 starting price](https://substack.com/redirect/8a042787-9814-4357-8452-b4d72958d5bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Ford Motor announced Thursday that **[its new midsize electric pickup truck called the Fathom will start at $28,350.](https://substack.com/redirect/5b877957-e153-4aa6-8a4c-c065821f0312?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Preorders begin early 2027 with deliveries expected later in 2027.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8a042787-9814-4357-8452-b4d72958d5bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **First UEV platform vehicle:** The Fathom is the first vehicle to be built using Ford's Universal Electric Vehicle platform, key to bringing Model e from losses to breakeven by 2029.
* **Total price target hit:** Destination and delivery charges of $1,595 bring the starting price to $29,945, meeting the $30,000 mark the automaker had long promised.
* **Timeline and production:** Preorders for the five-passenger truck start in early 2027 with deliveries later that year at the Louisville Assembly Plant using new processes.
* **Context of EV slowdown:** The push comes despite a massive slowdown in EV adoption, elimination of U.S. incentives, and $19.5 billion in prior restructuring charges related to electric vehicles.

# [CHEERS! Diageo shares jump 7% on $1 billion savings plan](https://substack.com/redirect/8a042787-9814-4357-8452-b4d72958d5bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Diageo shares jumped nearly 7.3% Thursday after the world's biggest spirits maker **[unveiled a $1 billion three-year savings plan,](https://substack.com/redirect/78fe8911-1475-49dd-a2b0-57352a0da751?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with related restructuring costs totaling $1.2 billion to turn around the business.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8a042787-9814-4357-8452-b4d72958d5bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Organic sales decline:** Organic net sales for the year ending June 30 declined 2% to $19.643 billion while adjusted operating profit rose 2% to $5.7 billion largely from cost savings.
* **North America weakness:** CEO Dave Lewis noted hard work ahead particularly in North America where organic sales declined 8.4% in the year ending June 30 for the company.
* **World Cup sales boost:** FIFA World Cup helped drive ready-to-drink beverages and cocktails sales up 35.1% largely from Casamigos ready-to-serve and strong Bulleit and Ketel One sales.
* **Strategic priorities set:** Key priorities include keeping core brands competitive with consumer trends, putting customers central to decisions, and building a more agile efficient operating framework.

* * *
* * *
# [Aussie airline to start charging for overhead bag storage](https://substack.com/redirect/8a042787-9814-4357-8452-b4d72958d5bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Budget Australian airline Jetstar will begin charging passengers **[between $18 and $37 for storing large carry-on bags in overhead compartments](https://substack.com/redirect/6b33b06d-31eb-4aaa-b105-f5a9fbd51dcd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** starting in February 2027.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8a042787-9814-4357-8452-b4d72958d5bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **New fee structure set:** The priority carry-on fee of A$25 to A$52 depending on route includes early boarding access for bags up to 22 pounds on one-way flights.
* **Weight limit removed:** Bags stowed in compartments will no longer be weighed by staff before boarding, removing the current 15-pound limit for those who pay the fee.
* **Free underseat allowance:** Passengers can still stow smaller bags such as a purse, laptop bag or backpack meeting measurements under the seat in front of them free.
* **Efficiency goal stated:** CEO Stephanie Tully said the change will make better use of overhead locker space, streamline boarding and help more flights depart on time.

My opponent just dropped out | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136752725/638479219/-478934984?refcode=em-8.6.26-all&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjAyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMWY3OWFlOC1iZDkxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=p1tM64TQKrtdrFmCNf4dpxuYuJh-U827dkxanh4FZGc=) Friend, our opponent just dropped out of the race and I’m calling on you for support. I grew up on our family farm in Fairview, and I have spent my life learning what it means to show up, keep going, and take responsibility when things are hard. After Hurricane Helene, that has felt even more true. Recovery is still underway, and folks across this district cannot afford chaos or indifference. That is why I am running. I believe Western North Carolina deserves representation grounded in decency, service, and neighborliness, especially when the road ahead is unclear. **And just as plainly, I want to say this.** I stand with survivors of sexual abuse and harassment. The allegations against Edwards are serious, and they deserve to be handled with care and integrity. My heart goes out to the young women who took these roles to serve our community. This campaign has never been about any one person. It’s always been about Western North Carolina and our communities getting the leadership and representation we deserve. That has not changed. We are building a strong grassroots team to defeat whoever is on the ballot. It’s time to give Western North Carolina the representation we deserve. [**I’m asking you to stay close in the days ahead. We are going to need people who are paying attention and staying engaged. name: David Hogg
subject: They’re (still) pissed at me
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
An update on our fight.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260806-1&t=1&akid=3828%2E587540%2Eh950N-)
Peter, last year, I sent out an email with the subject line: _“They are pissed at me.”_
After I was elected Vice Chair of the DNC last year, I became the center of controversy when Leaders We Deserve pledged to make a major investment in challenging asleep-at-the-wheel, ineffective Democratic incumbents in safe seats in 2026.
This mission cost me my role at the DNC, but I wasn’t about to bow down to a party establishment that wanted to stick to the same old failed playbook that had already lost to Donald Trump twice. Because we cannot be the real opposition voters are looking for if our politicians are too cowardly or comfortable to fight back.
Fast forward to now, and our plan is already paying off. On Tuesday, **Donavan McKinney became the first Leaders We Deserve candidate of the cycle to unseat an incumbent Democrat** who was failing his constituents time and again.
We’re showing up every day and doing this work because we’re done begging for table scraps from the establishment. We’re flipping the table over and rebuilding it.
And that’s why I can guarantee you this: **They are _still_ pissed at me, Peter.**
But I don’t really care. If it makes them mad that we’re fighting for a stronger Democratic Party that can not only stand up to Trump and the Republicans, but also win again by actually offering voters something new, then so be it. I have bigger things to worry about than hurt feelings. Our country is at stake, and the establishment isn’t willing to do what it takes to save it.
**If you were a supporter through all this and are still with us, thank you for sticking by us and turning that dream into a reality. If you’re new to this fight, we’re so glad to have you on the team. This movement is growing by the day, and I firmly believe we have what it takes to reshape the Democratic Party.**
**[Will you make a $5 donation to keep powering this game-changing work?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260806_1_pissed.eUPrbt&refcode=em20260806-3828&amount=5&t=2&akid=3828%2E587540%2Eh950N-)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260806_1_pissed.eUPrbt&amount=5&refcode=em20260806-3828&t=3&akid=3828%2E587540%2Eh950N-)**
Thank you,
David
P.S. You can look back at where we started by reading my original email below — **[and then pitch in $5 to the fight.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260806_1_pissed.eUPrbt&refcode=em20260806-3828&amount=5&t=4&akid=3828%2E587540%2Eh950N-)**
_— Message from David Hogg. Sent April 2025 —_
Peter, I’m always direct in my emails. Papering over bad news doesn’t help us win.
So I’ll get right to the point — it is a hell of a lot harder to slow, derail, and stop Trump from crashing the economy, disappearing people, and leading our country into ruin with a weak Democratic Party.
With a 26% approval rating, that is where we are right now. If the midterms were held today, we would lose.
And yeah, a few members of the old-school Democratic establishment are pissed at me for calling us weak. They can’t understand why Leaders We Deserve would consider primarying complacent, ineffective congressmen who are asleep at the wheel during the most consequential moments in our political history.
In today’s party politics, there’s an unwritten rule. If you win a seat, it’s yours for life. No one serious in your party will challenge you. That is a culture we have to break.
I am doing this so that we have a stronger party. We stand a significantly better chance at defeating MAGA if we can build a more effective Democratic Party that gives voters a real alternative — a vision for the future they believe in.
The answer lies in building the party we all know we could be. A party that restores people's faith in Democracy by using it to revive the American Dream through lowering costs and fighting special interests. To do that requires serious change, though.
Yes, there are incredible Democratic leaders that we already have who are stepping up. But unfortunately there are far too many who are asleep at the wheel and completely failing to meet the moment. That is unacceptable.
We cannot recycle the same playbook and expect different results. That’s why Leaders We Deserve is launching a mission to usher in the next generation by:
* Primarying asleep-at-the-wheel Democrats in deep blue seats. It might seem counterintuitive to do this in blue seats, but people decide their votes based on what they think about Democrats and Republicans overall. The weak, ineffective, out-of-touch members of Congress are a liability for us all.
* Supporting young, bold Democrats running in tight red-to-blue races.
* Making sure the next generation of leaders in tough districts have our full support in flipping Republican seats and increasing Democratic majorities at the State and National level.

When we challenge the status quo, some incumbents will rise to the occasion and emerge stronger, reminded of who they serve. Others will demonstrate exactly why they need to be replaced. Either way, the party gets stronger, and the American people win.
This initiative will be ambitious. This action plan for a renewed, stronger Democratic Party comes down to each of the people reading this email doing what they can with what they have. If we all rise to that level, the plan will work.
I know that everyone reading this email isn’t in a position to donate. That is okay. And I believe we can fund this effort successfully in a truly progressive way. Here’s how:
**⇢HIGH EARNERS:** If you have done well and can afford it, please consider investing more for those who can’t. **[Click to donate $1,000, $500 or $100 or as much as you can to Leaders We Deserve.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/5748?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260806_1_pissed.KeM0YU&refcode=em20260806-3828&t=5&akid=3828%2E587540%2Eh950N-)**
**⇢MEDIUM EARNERS:** Give what you can. What’s more important is that we’re all in this together. If thousands of people give small amounts each month, this plan will still work. **[Click to donate $25 — or $5 a month — to Leaders We Deserve.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/5783?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260806_1_pissed.yhFy6X&refcode=em20260806-3828&t=6&akid=3828%2E587540%2Eh950N-)**
**⇢EVERYONE ELSE:** If you are not in a position to donate, that’s okay. We each have a role to play in this plan, and yours might be to do all of the free things you can do. Get active on social media. Tell your friends about what we’re doing. Forward this email around. You are just as important in this fight.
We’ll check in periodically with you on our progress here. But I really believe that today we’re going to make a big step in the right direction for our party and our country.
Thank you for reading, especially a long email like this one. It means a lot to me personally to be in this work and this fight with teammates as dedicated as you. The energy I draw from people like you is what keeps me fighting every day.
Thank you,
David Hogg
Leaders We Deserve

clean_body: Federal agents are in our cities monitoring everyday people. Organizing is how we protect our freedoms. | | | Peter, the presence of federal agents can dismantle the fabric of a community’s safety overnight. Last fall, when a federal task force was launched in Memphis, immigration enforcement was never named as a goal. But over the next 10 months, the task force was secretly repurposed and weaponized into a sweeping immigration crackdown.1 Fear rippled through the city as federal agents used routine traffic stops to detain working people and separate families: parents pulled children from school, people stopped going to work, and medical appointments were skipped.1 Memphis is not alone. Federal agents are systematically targeting working people, U.S. citizens and immigrants alike.2 Public records released this month show federal agents recorded the license plates of people at a protest and logged their names and home addresses in a digital evidence system.2 One man was documented for parking in a public lot. Another for photographing a bus he mistook for an immigration transport vehicle.2 This is an assault on the rights of all Americans. When the government tracks how we gather, speak, or move throughout our own neighborhoods and cities, our fundamental First Amendment freedoms shrink. Instead of tackling the rising costs of groceries, housing, gas, and healthcare, those in power are spending our taxpayer dollars to violate our rights while protecting the interests of billionaires and political insiders who profit from a multi-billion-dollar enforcement apparatus. _**The good news:**_ A federal judge knocked President Trump's executive order ending federal funding for NPR and PBS, saying it violated the broadcasters' First Amendment rights.

_**The bad news:**_ Trump cut $1.1 billion for public media outlets that he and Congress had earlier agreed to, **and this ruling doesn’t automatically guarantee that broadcasters will receive the funding they need to function.**

Crucially, this ruling does open the door for Congress to resume funding for public media in the future.

That’s why it’s vital that grassroots Democrats like you join us in supporting Public Broadcasting stations like NPR and PBS!

Hi Peter, Today marks 61 years since the landmark Voting Rights Act was signed, giving long-overdue voter protections to Black Americans.

The 1960s may be bygone, but the Jim Crow-era voting bans aimed to disenfranchise communities of color remain prevalent in our nation, albeit under a different guise. Donald Trump’s Supreme Court has gutted the Voting Rights Act in a shameful and unacceptable attack on underrepresented voters across the country. Using the Supreme Court as their tool, Republicans are weakening voting rights, targeting Black members of Congress and Black-majority districts, and making it harder for millions of Americans to have their voices heard. And here in North Carolina, new rules on voter ID, mail-in voting and polling place access are part of a broader wave of changes that could make voting more difficult. From manipulating our voting maps to dilute the voting power of communities of color, rolling back mail-in and early voting options often utilized by many voters of color, and gutting the Voting Rights Act — **Americans are still facing unethical voter suppression tactics that aim to silence voices at the ballot box and beyond.** I’m in Congress fighting for a country where democracy can flourish and where the fundamental right to vote is protected for all Americans — but we must stand up to protect the promise of our democracy and the right to vote for all Americans. **[Democracy is nothing without teamwork, Peter. Will you stand with me by adding your name to our petition and ensuring every voter is heard?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136753283/638480389/1540432828?source=VF_EM_FR_080626_B1_VRA&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTc5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZmQ4YzQ0ZC1iZjkxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XWMNyBmcQ8KbF9OAcZ319qNPinJUw6DJ5qto-vQYXuM=&emci=29d8c44d-bf91-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=2fd8c44d-bf91-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=799895)** | | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136753284/638480390/1540432828?source=VF_EM_FR_080626_B1_VRA&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTc5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZmQ4YzQ0ZC1iZjkxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XWMNyBmcQ8KbF9OAcZ319qNPinJUw6DJ5qto-vQYXuM=&emci=29d8c44d-bf91-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=2fd8c44d-bf91-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=799895)

subject: We Have the Oil. So Why Are We Paying More?
body:
The math is simple: America has the oil, but we need the refining capacity to put America First.

| | | | | | | [VIEW THIS EMAIL IN BROWSER](https://mailchi.mp/a2016a04fa7b/to-my-dad-on-fathers-day-2375659?e=3cb50a0604)

| |
**Refine baby, Refine** _By Austin Sidwell
_ "They're making too much money based on a shortage..."
President Donald Trump admonished oil companies this week in the midst of the on again, off again conflictin Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. An easy target of scorn with the national average price per gallon hovering around $4.09. Public disdain is high. But the number ofoptions seems incredibly low.

The establishment in DC does a great job of pointing fingers but not offering alternatives. So let's do a little math. Where does the US stand as far as oil production, oil refinement, and do we produce enough oil to take care of our own?
The United States is the 4th largest exporter of oil in the world. We're behind Saudi Arabia, Russia and Canada, but higher than the UAE, Kuwait, Iraq and Iran. While this may be news to many people there's something even more impressive. We actually export more oil than we import. We export 10.7M barrels of oil while we import 7.9M barrels of oil. In other words, if we used our own oil and didn't import anything, we'd still have excess to sell in the world market.
A country of 89 million people who don't own, nor can they claim any sovereignty over a waterway, should not dictate affordability in our country! We have the capability of producing enough oil to take care of our own. Which begs the questions of why aren't we? Where are we deficient in the economic food chain relating to oil, refinement and transportation?
This brings us to the crux of the discussion, refineries. While the US has 132 refineries nationwide, we don't have enough. Comparatively, the bulk of refinement is done in other countries around the world. While we have supply, demand, we're not at full capacity to refine what we produce. We have elected officials in Washington who've neglected to look at the underlying issue.
Solution:refine baby refine.

We don't need a government program or to fork over tax dollars to create a pork project to drive industry leaders, we need tax incentives. We need to get out of the way of oil companies willing to invest in this country. Oil refineries employeehundreds of American workers, thousands of American workers are needed to build the facilities, and ultimately American taxpayers will pay less at the pump when we don't have to factor in transportation and shipping costs. Refineries and holding on to our own supply of oil places us in a truly unique situation which cries "America First."
When the math doesn't math, our elected officials tell us it's somebody else's problem. But the math is simple, we consume 20% of the world's oil, but we refine about 15%. We can do better. We can at least tell the world, we're a sovereign nation and we won't let anyone dictate our economy. The war with Iran is about more than oil. But while we fight against extremism, we can't let terrorists win at the pump.

clean_body: The math is simple: America has the oil, but we need the refining capacity to put America First. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Refine baby, Refine By Austin Sidwell "They're making too much money based on a shortage..." President Donald Trump admonished oil companies this week in the midst of the on again, off again conflictin Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. An easy target of scorn with the national average price per gallon hovering around $4.09. Public disdain is high. But the number ofoptions seems incredibly low. The establishment in DC does a great job of pointing fingers but not offering alternatives. So let's do a little math. Where does the US stand as far as oil production, oil refinement, and do we produce enough oil to take care of our own? The United States is the 4th largest exporter of oil in the world. We're behind Saudi Arabia, Russia and Canada, but higher than the UAE, Kuwait, Iraq and Iran. While this may be news to many people there's something even more impressive. We actually export more oil than we import. We export 10.7M barrels of oil while we import 7.9M barrels of oil. In other words, if we used our own oil and didn't import anything, we'd still have excess to sell in the world market. A country of 89 million people who don't own, nor can they claim any sovereignty over a waterway, should not dictate affordability in our country! We have the capability of producing enough oil to take care of our own. Which begs the questions of why aren't we? Where are we deficient in the economic food chain relating to oil, refinement and transportation? This brings us to the crux of the discussion, refineries. While the US has 132 refineries nationwide, we don't have enough. Comparatively, the bulk of refinement is done in other countries around the world. While we have supply, demand, we're not at full capacity to refine what we produce. We have elected officials in Washington who've neglected to look at the underlying issue. Solution:refine baby refine. We don't need a government program or to fork over tax dollars to create a pork project to drive industry leaders, we need tax incentives. We need to get out of the way of oil companies willing to invest in this country. Oil refineries employeehundreds of American workers, thousands of American workers are needed to build the facilities, and ultimately American taxpayers will pay less at the pump when we don't have to factor in transportation and shipping costs. Refineries and holding on to our own supply of oil places us in a truly unique situation which cries "America First." When the math doesn't math, our elected officials tell us it's somebody else's problem. But the math is simple, we consume 20% of the world's oil, but we refine about 15%. We can do better. We can at least tell the world, we're a sovereign nation and we won't let anyone dictate our economy. The war with Iran is about more than oil. But while we fight against extremism, we can't let terrorists win at the pump. | | P.S. The special primary is Tuesday, August 11. name: Tobias Read
subject: The 61st anniversary of the Voting Rights Act
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
Friend,
Today marks the 61st anniversary of the Voting Rights Act.
Sixty-one years ago, ordinary Americans did extraordinary things. They marched. They endured beatings, arrests, intimidation, and worse. And then continued to march so that future generations would have a voice in our democracy.
They carried the torch.
For decades, the Voting Rights Act stood as one of our nation's greatest civil rights achievements.
But over the last thirteen years, we've watched those protections steadily erode.
First, the Supreme Court dismantled the Act's preclearance protections in Shelby County v. Holder.
Then, in Brnovich, it made challenges to discriminatory voting laws even harder.
And this year, in Louisiana v. Callais, the Court dealt another devastating blow by sharply limiting Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, making it significantly harder to protect the voting power of Black communities and other historically marginalized voters.
Across the South, we're already seeing the consequences. Black voting power is being dismantled. Districts are being carved up, communities are being divided, and politicians are choosing their voters instead of letting voters choose their leaders.
That's exactly why the fight for the Voting Rights Act is far from over.
History has taught us something important:
Rights are never guaranteed.
Every generation has to decide whether it will defend them.
The generation that marched in Selma and fought for the Voting Rights Act passed the torch to us.
Now it's our turn to carry it.
As your Secretary of State, I don't see protecting the freedom to vote as just another responsibility of the office.
I see it as a calling.
I believe every eligible voter deserves to cast a ballot freely. Every lawful vote deserves to be counted. And every Oregonian deserves confidence that our elections are fair, secure, and accessible.
But none of us can fight this fight alone.
If you believe the fight for voting rights didn't end in 1965—and won't end in 2026—I'm asking you to stand with me today. Will you make a contribution to help us continue the work that generations before us began? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
The torch is in our hands now.
Let's carry it forward.
Thank you,
Tobias
Secretary of State

But a lot of it was a shot in the dark. One thing I knew for sure: I would need a massive team behind me. More than a year and a half later, we’ve built that team. Last quarter more than 90% of our contributions came from grassroots gifts of less than $100. And with that support, we’ve built an operation that has turned this Lean-R district into a tossup. I’m incredibly proud of that, and I hope you are too. For 250 years our nation has gone through really dark times, really hard chapters. In these extraordinary moments, ordinary people rose up and chose to live with courage. They knew America and our democracy are worth fighting for. subject: 47th. Out of 50.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Garrity for PA * 4075 Linglestown Rd PMB 119 * Harrisburg, PA 17112-1020 * USA
body:
Pennsylvania just dropped NINE spots in the national rankings. Shapiro says his work is "paying off."

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/aFSbKTeKjh_?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
| | | | | | Peter,

For nearly a year, I’ve been traveling across this Commonwealth telling you that Pennsylvania is falling behind.
In nearly every speech I’ve given, I’ve cited the same numbers: 38th economically, 39th in education, 41st overall.
Last week, we found out it’s getting worse.
[**According to U.S. News & World Report, Pennsylvania’s economy now ranks 47th out of 50 states in the nation. That’s a drop of 9 spots.**](https://us.list-manage.com/gAF_MmK4lNS?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
47th. Out of 50. Only three states in America have a worse-performing economy than ours right now.
And what does Josh Shapiro say? He says his work is “paying off.”
**Paying off for who?**
Not for the families struggling to make ends meet. Not for the small business owners drowning in taxes. Not for the parents watching their kids fall behind in schools that aren’t working.
**Here are the facts:**
📉 Pennsylvania’s economy has dropped from 38th to 47th in the nation under Shapiro
📚 Nearly 7 in 10 eighth graders can’t read at grade level — yet Shapiro refuses to opt into a federal scholarship program that even liberal governors in New York and Colorado have embraced
🌉 Nearly 3,000 bridges across the Commonwealth are structurally deficient — our infrastructure earns a C-minus grade
💸 Pennsylvania has the 5th highest tax burden in the entire country, making it harder to raise a family, start a business, and build a life here
Josh Shapiro talks a lot about one bridge his administration repaired in Philadelphia. One bridge. Meanwhile, thousands of bridges across this state are crumbling, our kids can’t read, and our economy is in free-fall.
That’s not leadership. That’s a press release.
But here’s the good news:
**It doesn’t have to be this way.**
As Governor, I won’t just talk about Pennsylvania’s problems. I have a plan to solve them.
🏡 **Deliver meaningful property tax relief** so seniors can stay in the homes they spent a lifetime building.
⚡ **Lower electric and utility bills** by unleashing Pennsylvania energy, eliminating unnecessary taxes on utilities, and ending costly government mandates.
💰 **Reduce insurance costs** by cutting red tape, increasing competition, and cracking down on fraud.
💊 **Lower prescription drug costs** by taking on the middlemen driving up prices and strengthening programs that help seniors afford the medications they need.
❤️ **Support family caregivers** so more Pennsylvanians can age at home with dignity and independence.
📉 **Restore fiscal discipline** in Harrisburg so today's overspending doesn't become tomorrow's tax increase.
That’s what a turnaround looks like.
Not more speeches.
Not more photo ops.
Not more excuses.
Real solutions that make Pennsylvania more affordable, more competitive, and a place where our children choose to stay instead of feeling like they need to leave.
47th is not who we are.
And it certainly isn’t where we’re going.
With your help, we’re going to turn Pennsylvania around.
Onward,

subject: 61 years ago, they fought for your right to vote.

https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vg4lgad?refcode=em080626 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vg4lgad?refcode=em080626]
Peter,
Sixty-one years ago, the Voting Rights Act was signed into law. It wasn't handed to us. It was fought for in Texas, by Texans.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vg4lgad?refcode=em080626 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vg4lgad?refcode=em080626]
In 1944, Houston dentist Lonnie E. Smith sued Texas for turning him away from the Democratic primary — and won. Smith v. Allwright gave the vote to millions of Americans.
President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Voting Rights Act into law, knowing it would cost his party the South.
Congressman Kika de la Garza was the only Hispanic member of Congress to sign the original VRA and worked tirelessly to extend it.
State Senator Barbara Jordan passed laws in Texas to expand its protections to Latino and Spanish-speaking voters.
And activist Willie Velásquez built a movement around a motto that still rings true today: Su Voto Es Su Voz — Your Vote Is Your Voice.
They set us on the path. Sixty-one years later, the fight they started is ours to finish. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vg4lgad?refcode=em080626]
SUPPORT VIKKI IN THIS FIGHT [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vg4lgad?refcode=em080626]
Dan Patrick, on the other hand, is the reason Texas now ranks 46th in the nation for voting access.
* He has banned drive-thru voting.
* He has restricted mail-in drop boxes.
* He presided over the removal of 2.1 million Texans from the voter rolls.
* He championed Trump’s redistricting maps, drawn to dilute Black and Brown voting power.
Power for him – but not for the people. This is a man who has collected nearly $1 billion in campaign contributions (a record for any Texas politician) from the billionaires, corporate PACs, and special interests who benefit most when fewer Texans are able to vote.
Dan Patrick is selling out Texans, and we cannot afford another session of him putting donors before democracy. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vg4lgad?refcode=em080626]
In 2021, I stood against his voter suppression bills. In 2025, I pushed back against his mid-decade redistricting scheme and I introduced the Empowering Texans Ballot Initiative Act to let citizens put an independent, nonpartisan redistricting commission on the ballot themselves.
We don’t need politicians drawing new maps whenever they feel their grip on power slipping. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vg4lgad?refcode=em080626]
The right to vote is not something you earn – it’s a fundamental democratic right.
As Lieutenant Governor, I will make it a priority to pass bills that protect your vote and your voice.
Dan Patrick has used the power of this office against you.
I will use it for you.
This moment demands that we stand together and protect our Constitutional Rights. Will you fight with me? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vg4lgad?refcode=em080626]

**MEMORANDUM FROM TYLER BOWYER, EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR**
* * *

Friend,
---
Early voting is almost here and I want to give you a direct update from the ground.
Starting now, Turning Point PAC will be shifting into higher and higher gears every week as we fund the immediate surge of ballot-chasers across America.
This week: **Arizona. Nevada. Michigan. Pennsylvania. Ohio. Indiana. Wisconsin. New Hampshire.**
We've been on calls with our teams in every one of these states this week. The energy is there. More chasers are being recruited, and trained. The infrastructure we've been building since January is ready.
[What we need now is the resources to run it at full speed](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjF9AAwAAAAAAjAzv_Fuj4dZCjEg0auRJkE1CGc1CfDa9RYS5rcrc0KwG7AKzWdVv1P6oefFqixhweT94PHBVKzQiHMlvXMJ7_ZPeLtWmZdrBixFqhnhxg) — because early voting begins in fewer than **eight weeks** and there is no recovery window if we come up short.

[BACK THE SURGE](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjF9AAwAAAAAAjAzv_FvIEopF8D7RUzvKCIjOOuBS9XZLTJU-XUsfJWz754LUouUrMNgvBepPURbOH1lHtGVhfLi77y8Og-RSX87srp31JVdGpwWu_4X8w)

Let me be direct about what this moment means.
Midterm races are decided by turnout margins that would look like rounding errors in a presidential race. A few thousand votes in a handful of swing districts in Michigan or Pennsylvania or Nevada — that's the difference between keeping the House and handing Hakeem Jeffries and his communist caucus the gavel!
Our ballot-chasers are in those districts **right now.**
But a ground operation at this scale — eight states, hundreds of chasers, sustained through eight weeks of early voting — costs real money. Every day we're underfunded is a day we're leaving doors unknocked and ballots uncollected in districts we cannot afford to lose.
I've never asked more urgently than I'm asking right now. **[Will you back the surge?](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjF9AAwAAAAAAjAzv_FwXdtpg8rf6th4UpouaE2h9qybJ0pZ-rmFMfxG-uG4FCIvIJEYgRZo2286qm-cUaVOv48SmSVE93_EMkSLupodYuYbgZkTV_MHVg)**

**[No contribution is too small. $10, $50, $100. Every dollar you can spare DIRECTLY supports ballot chasing and puts points on the scoreboard on Election Day. Will you help?](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjF9AAwAAAAAAjAzv_Fy4AjlzFWO3MuDH5VeGtUGfQhOz1-geDt7Pgb0pP-QAAuijWVJQjK257apcvOraG_534_O3kvqWjxHZw6Vr-oeKPIUv1RhSliozQ)**
Eight states. Eight weeks. Everything we've built comes down to this.
For America,

**Tyler Bowyer**
Executive Director
Turning Point PAC

body:
190,000 voters. $0.36 each. Here's how we win.

| | | | | |
---
| | | | | | Hello Peter,

I'll be honest with you, because that's how I've always run this campaign.
We are at the moment where this race is won or lost — not in a debate hall, but on doorsteps, on phone lines, and in the text messages that reach voters across Ohio's 8th District. And right now, we need your help to keep that work going.
Here's what's at stake. After the October 2025 redistricting, Hamilton County became the new majority of our district. That changed everything. Since 2020, we've closed the margin here by roughly **12 points** — not by accident, but by showing up, cycle after cycle, and talking with voters no one else bothered to reach.
Our path to victory runs through **190,000 votes**. We know exactly who those voters are, where they live, and how to reach them. And because we run one of the most disciplined, efficient voter-contact operations in the state, we can reach a voter for as little as **$0.36**.
Think about what that means:
* **$36** helps us reach **100 voters** with our message
* **$108** puts our message in front of **300 households**
* **$250** funds an entire afternoon of calls and texts from our volunteer team
* **$500** helps us hold the line in a key precinct where this race will be decided

Every single dollar you give goes directly into the two things that win congressional races: **contacting voters and getting our message out.** Not overhead. Not noise. Voter contact.
And our message is one worth fighting for — protecting Social Security and Medicare, defending voting rights and workers' rights, expanding affordable healthcare, safeguarding women's reproductive freedom, supporting our small businesses, and opening the doors of technology and opportunity to communities that have been left out for too long.
We have the plan. We have the volunteers. We have the momentum. What we need now is the fuel to finish the job.
**Will you chip in today to help us reach the voters who will decide this election?**

That changed everything. Since 2020, we've closed the margin here by roughly 12 points — not by accident, but by showing up, cycle after cycle, and talking with voters no one else bothered to reach. Our path to victory runs through 190,000 votes. We know exactly who those voters are, where they live, and how to reach them. And because we run one of the most disciplined, efficient voter-contact operations in the state, we can reach a voter for as little as $0.36. Think about what that means: $36 helps us reach 100 voters with our message $108 puts our message in front of 300 households $250 funds an entire afternoon of calls and texts from our volunteer team $500 helps us hold the line in a key precinct where this race will be decided Every single dollar you give goes directly into the two things that win congressional races: contacting voters and getting our message out. Not overhead. Not noise. Voter contact. And our message is one worth fighting for — protecting Social Security and Medicare, defending voting rights and workers' rights, expanding affordable healthcare, safeguarding women's reproductive freedom, supporting our small businesses, and opening the doors of technology and opportunity to communities that have been left out for too long. We have the plan. We have the volunteers. We have the momentum. What we need now is the fuel to finish the job. Will you chip in today to help us reach the voters who will decide this election? | | | | | | Whatever you can give — — it reaches real voters and moves us closer to victory. And I am grateful for every bit of it. Thank you for standing with us. This is our district, our moment, and our movement — and we're going to win it together. With gratitude and hope, Dr. Vanessa Enoch Democratic Nominee for Congress, Ohio's 8th District | | | | | | | P.S. The next few weeks are when campaigns are won. Every dollar you give right now is worth more than a dollar given later, because it lets us reach voters while there's still time to earn their vote. body:
Together we can fight back against the chaos coming from Washington.
| | | [](https://go.dscc.org/go/23722?amount=7&t=4&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FM-20260806-AdamHamilton-AdamHamiltonNotAPoliticianTandem-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FM-20260806-AdamHamilton-AdamHamiltonNotAPoliticianTandem-Pros-sl1&akid=25311%2E9716520%2EYHQG1c)
I'm a lifelong pastor here in Kansas, and I never thought I'd run for office - but polling has shown I'm running neck and neck with incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall in the race for U.S. Senate here.

I just became the Democratic nominee, and I hope you'll give me a chance to explain why your support today would be so impactful - but if you're already on board, **[you can click here to split a donation between my campaign and the DSCC to help us kick off our general election campaign and win in places like Kansas.](https://go.dscc.org/go/23722?amount=7&t=5&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FM-20260806-AdamHamilton-AdamHamiltonNotAPoliticianTandem-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FM-20260806-AdamHamilton-AdamHamiltonNotAPoliticianTandem-Pros-sl1&akid=25311%2E9716520%2EYHQG1c)**

Let me backtrack a bit. I've spent my life trying to serve the people of my community. I'm a fifth‐generation Kansan, and I've been a pastor at the church my wife, LaVon, and I started for more than three decades.

We started with four people, my wife and our two daughters, in a funeral home chapel. It was a place for people who were hurting or had questions or doubts. Now, the church is the largest in Kansas. Even all these years later, I'm proud to say that mission hasn't changed.

Today, I see Kansas families hurting under the weight of rising costs and selfish, chaotic leadership from Washington. I've spent my life not as a politician, but as a servant - and right now, the best way that I feel I can serve is by running for the U.S. Senate.

Our biggest hurdle is making sure we have the resources to compete. Polls show this race will be competitive, and I'm going to rely on grassroots supporters like yourself to help us keep up the momentum.

I'm not taking donations from corporate PACs, unlike my opponent Sen. Roger Marshall. I'm counting on real people like you to fund this campaign one donation at a time - because everyday people are who I plan to serve in the Senate.

**[So what do you say? If you're ready to change the status quo in Washington, win in places like Kansas, and send an independent‐minded Democrat, I hope you'll chip in any amount right now to support my campaign and the DSCC.](https://go.dscc.org/go/23722?amount=7&t=6&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FM-20260806-AdamHamilton-AdamHamiltonNotAPoliticianTandem-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FM-20260806-AdamHamilton-AdamHamiltonNotAPoliticianTandem-Pros-sl1&akid=25311%2E9716520%2EYHQG1c)**

body:
It’s time to take back the House and hold this administration accountable.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3645%2E21716%2ENhAJ66)
**This week, the Senate Judiciary Committee voted to advance Todd Blanche’s nomination to be Attorney General** — the same guy who said he thinks of himself not as the people’s lawyer, but as Donald Trump’s _personal_ lawyer.
Time and time again, Blanche has shown a stunning lack of moral clarity. He has:
* Led the cover-up of the Epstein files.

* Designed Trump’s $1.8 billion taxpayer-funded slush fund to pay January 6th rioters and convicted criminals.

* Granted Trump and his family and business a “Super Pardon” that shields them for life from any federal investigation, audit, lawsuit, or prosecution for violations of federal law.

When Senate Republicans vote to confirm him, they’re choosing loyalty to Donald Trump over the rule of law and the American people.

I have good news and bad news. I am going to start with the good, because I think you deserve to hear it. **July was the strongest grassroots fundraising month of this entire campaign.** While Sabato's Crystal Ball was moving 14 races toward Democrats. While James Talarico's billionaire backers were writing $10 million checks. While the national environment was shifting against Republicans at every turn, Texas conservatives showed up in a way that I will never forget. You gave more in July than in any month since this campaign began. Not because a single mega-donor wrote a massive check. Because thousands of grassroots conservatives across this state and this country decided that Texas was worth fighting for. That is the good news. And it is genuinely great news. **Now here is the bad news.** **Fox News just released a new poll showing James Talarico leading me 51% to 48%. This is Fox News. Not a Democratic pollster. Not a liberal outlet._Fox News_. And their poll shows Talarico over 50% for the first time in this race.** Here is what the numbers show. Talarico has 98% of Democrats. He has 68% of independents. And 24% of non-MAGA Republicans are supporting him. That last number is the one that concerns me most. Nearly one in four Republicans who did not back President Trump is currently planning to vote for a Democrat who believes God is nonbinary, calls the American flag a complicated symbol, and wants a welcome mat at the southern border. **_I am not going to sugarcoat this. These numbers are serious._** But here is what I know. The margin of error on the Fox News poll is plus or minus 3 points. This race is not over. Among undecided voters, more lean toward me than toward Talarico. And the grassroots momentum we built in July proves that when conservatives show up, we can compete. clean_body: I have good news and bad news... I have good news and bad news... | | | | | | | Fellow Patriot, I have good news and bad news. I am going to start with the good, because I think you deserve to hear it. July was the strongest grassroots fundraising month of this entire campaign. While Sabato's Crystal Ball was moving 14 races toward Democrats. While James Talarico's billionaire backers were writing $10 million checks. While the national environment was shifting against Republicans at every turn, Texas conservatives showed up in a way that I will never forget. You gave more in July than in any month since this campaign began. Not because a single mega-donor wrote a massive check. Because thousands of grassroots conservatives across this state and this country decided that Texas was worth fighting for. That is the good news. And it is genuinely great news. Now here is the bad news. Fox News just released a new poll showing James Talarico leading me 51% to 48%. This is Fox News. Not a Democratic pollster. Not a liberal outlet.Fox News. And their poll shows Talarico over 50% for the first time in this race. Here is what the numbers show. Talarico has 98% of Democrats. He has 68% of independents. And 24% of non-MAGA Republicans are supporting him. That last number is the one that concerns me most. Nearly one in four Republicans who did not back President Trump is currently planning to vote for a Democrat who believes God is nonbinary, calls the American flag a complicated symbol, and wants a welcome mat at the southern border. I am not going to sugarcoat this. These numbers are serious. But here is what I know. The margin of error on the Fox News poll is plus or minus 3 points. This race is not over. Among undecided voters, more lean toward me than toward Talarico. And the grassroots momentum we built in July proves that when conservatives show up, we can compete. The question is whether we can keep that momentum going into August... James Talarico has raised $70 million. He has the national media telling the story he wants told. What I have is you, and the strongest grassroots month this campaign has ever seen. Let us make August even stronger. Thank you, Ken Paxton P.S. -- Fox News showed Talarico at 51%. We have no time to coast in August. Please give right now and help us close the gap in August. () | | | Paid for by Ken Paxton for Senate | | PO BOX 3476 MCKINNEY, TX 75070 | | |

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. Derek, have you heard the news?
I’m teaming up with the Democratic National Committee to bring a grassroots supporter like _you_ to Washington, DC for a personal tour of one of my very favorite spots here — the Air and Space Museum.
**[DONATE ANY AMOUNT TO ENTER](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-Kelly-sweepstakes-2026?refcode=em_20260806_8432_fr&amount=7&refcode2=8432_22930333_EpPl_Q&akid=8432%2E22930333%2EEpPl_Q)**

[**But this is a limited-time opportunity, and I want to make sure you’ve secured your spot to enter. I know there’s a lot going on in the world. We’re living in a moment when the President wants us to feel divided and threatened.
Honestly, that’s a big part of why I want to show you around the Air and Space Museum. I spent over 50 days in orbit. Looking at Earth from the vastness of space was one of the most powerful reminders that _we’re all in this together_ , and that we can accomplish extraordinary things as a team.
So I’m counting on this team today. Your donation to the DNC not only gives you a chance to hang out with me, but it also helps Democrats build a people-powered movement capable of standing up to Trump and creating change.
Your support of the DNC means that you want to make the world a better place, for all of us. It would mean so much to me to thank you in person.

Hey, Peter. Roy here, following up on the General Election Supporter Survey my team sent over the weekend.
**Since we’re still 105 responses short of statistical significance, I decided to extend the deadline until 11:59 p.m. tomorrow night.**
Now that we’re exactly 90 days out from the election, we have to kick our efforts into high gear – but it won’t make a difference if those efforts fail to reflect the perspectives and priorities of folks on the ground, like you. So if you didn’t get a chance to share your thoughts with our campaign, I hope you’ll take a few minutes now to chime in.

Thanks in advance, Peter.

Roy Cooper

[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_su_pros_jtk993&amount=5&t=8&akid=2551%2E124072%2EaMBZGU)

Peter,

We’re sending out a survey today to a select number of supporters to gauge where our campaign is doing well and see where we might improve.
With less than 100 days until the election, we’re leaving nothing to chance – so today, we want to hear from you as one of our most committed supporters.
[**_Will you take just a minute to share your candid thoughts about this campaign and the race ahead in our General Election Supporter Survey?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/17299?code=email_su_pros_jtk993&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&t=9&akid=2551%2E124072%2EaMBZGU)

This campaign works best if the priorities, concerns and hopes for the future of all our supporters are driving our grassroots movement.
**That means the only way we’ll flip this seat blue for the first time since 2008 is with direct input from people like you, Peter.**
[**_Please take a minute to complete our new supporter survey tonight. We’d be grateful to have your insights, and we all look forward to hearing from you.**_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/17299?code=email_su_pros_jtk993&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=&t=11&akid=2551%2E124072%2EaMBZGU)

Team Cooper

Hi Peter, I want to talk to you directly about what is happening on the ground in Tennessee today. On Tuesday night, we watched something historic unfold across the country. In Missouri, voters resoundingly crushed a MAGA attempt to rig their citizen initiative process by a landslide. In Kansas, voters successfully blocked an extremist effort to pack their state Supreme Court. **Today, Tennessee is the next major frontline. We’ve been on the frontlines. ** To protect their unchecked, 15-year supermajority, Tennessee Republicans called a rushed special session to surgically carve up Memphis, our state's largest city and only majority-minority congressional district, into three separate pieces. They wanted total voter confusion. They wanted to dilute the power of the people. They want us to stay home and throw in the towel. **But they woke up a movement.** For the first time in decades, Tennessee Democrats have recruited a historic wave of candidates competing in all 95 counties to break their supermajority and deliver real results to make life better and more affordable for every family in Tennessee. We have trained over 300 new Tennessee organizers through our historic TNDP Organizing Hub and they have been working around the clock to clear up voter confusion, staff our voter protection hotline, and run our statewide GOTV phone banks. Our nominees will hit the ground running tomorrow morning to flip this state blue. We need to make sure they have the resources to compete in districts the Republicans never saw coming. Will you chip in $10 or $25 right now to fund our Election Day voter protection efforts and prove that Tennessee is worth fighting for? ➔
_**From Memphis to Mountain City, Tennessee Democrats are showing up to meet this moment with the urgency it demands.**_ Today, we choose our state and federal nominees for Governor, U.S. Senate, U.S. Congress, and the State House and Senate. It’s also the day we decide critical county races, including School Board, County Commission, and County Mayor, the local leaders who directly impact our daily lives. The table for Tennessee's future is set by the people who show up today; make sure nothing stands between you and the ballot box. _**📋 YOUR ELECTION DAY CHECKLIST:**_

Denver’s chief security officer quit July 2, alleging punishment for raising concerns
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hey friends,
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** DOJ lost its 20th straight [bid for Colorado's unredacted voter rolls](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), dismissed with prejudice, while separately suing the state over [in-state tuition for illegal immigrants](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Performance commissions [flagged 3 of 123 judges up for retention](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), though the statewide panel overrode one unfavorable local review. A Wyoming fugitive facing 72 child sex abuse charges, already once fled on a $250K bond, was [released again on a no-cost PR bond](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in Larimer County. Cyclosporiasis cases nearly [tripled statewide](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to 241 since January. And Denver's chief security officer resigned, alleging [retaliation for flagging layoffs and understaffing](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Steve Cortes cites 30-year mortgages at 6.78%, [up from 3.0% in 2021](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), saying immigration reform and ending war could ease inflation. Newt Gingrich flags [DSA's endorsement surge](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), including Colorado's Melat Kiros, who ousted 30-year incumbent Rep. DeGette while campaigning to abolish ICE. And Ari Armstrong critiques Gov. [Weiser's "blueprint" for pairing business talk with tax and regulatory hikes](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) while deferring to local control on housing.
This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, August 6, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Denver’s chief security officer quit July 2, alleging punishment for raising concerns](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
The chief security officer of the Denver Security Office sent a resignation email to more than a dozen recipients at 12:57 p.m. on July 2 — the day after his seven-year anniversary with the city — and used the letter to accuse General Services leaders of punishing him for raising concerns.
The letter was posted publicly on X by Do Better Denver, an anonymous account that publishes material about Denver city government. His name is redacted in the posted images. Rocky Mountain Voice has not independently authenticated the letter, and the city declined to confirm the resignation.
In the letter, he described being written up for speaking about layoffs, furloughs, frozen raises, increased workloads, and changes to CSA Rule 14. He received his first low annual rating in a 40-year career, he wrote, and was placed on a performance improvement plan. He said he had been mocked for his writing style, questioned for taking FMLA leave, and ridiculed for defending his team’s work.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Federal Judge Blocks DOJ Bid for Colorado’s Unredacted Voter Rolls](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [DENVER7](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_A federal judge sides with Colorado's Secretary of State, dealing the DOJ its 20th straight loss in its push for state-level voter data access._
* **DOJ's data request rejected:** U.S. District Judge Philip Brimmer dismissed with prejudice the Justice Department's lawsuit seeking unredacted Colorado voter data — including names, birthdates, addresses, and partial Social Security or driver's license numbers — ruling DOJ lacked a valid purpose for the request.
* **Part of a broader pattern:** The ruling marks the federal government's 20th consecutive court loss in its effort to obtain unredacted voter rolls from Colorado and 30 other states that declined to comply with the December request.
* **More election fights ahead:** Secretary of State Jena Griswold framed the ruling as a win against federal overreach, while the Trump administration's separate emergency appeal to limit mail-in ballots still awaits a Supreme Court decision expected later this month.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | AUGUST 4**
_DSA’s youth section trains students to organize on campus. What happens after graduation is its own story, one its own members describe directly. “YDSA’s job is to train socialists on campus and create a pipeline into DSA,” Dare Cima, a University of Louisville YDSA member, said at the organization’s national conference this spring._
__
**[Two measures. Two opposite answers. One Colorado income tax rate.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | AUGUST 3** _Colorado voters may face a choice in November between two measures that couldn’t disagree more about the state income tax. One would replace the flat rate with a graduated system and raise close to $2 billion a year. The other would make it illegal to raise the rate at all._

**[The Initiative Weapon: Look Up!](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 2** _We’ve spent a lot of time with nursery rhymes lately. Today, let’s trade Mother Goose for a swimsuit. Have you ever done something wonderfully weird? Nearly 14 years ago, while celebrating our twenty-fifth wedding anniversary, Sherrie and I traveled to Cozumel, Mexico. One morning we signed up for a snorkeling excursion in the beautiful Caribbean Sea._ __

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136761471/638501467/1641829122?refcode=ea.ad83af4f-cc91-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ms=ea.ad83af4f-cc91-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ5NTciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWQ4M2FmNGYtY2M5MS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZqelUU9yTjNvXj-Vb2e9RyDp0sBbcPfQV3aZnuOC6KM=) After college, I wanted to do something — _everything_ I could — to make a difference, and I quickly realized that change starts at home. After talking with Vermonters from all walks of life about the many issues we have to tackle, I concentrated on one project that became my focus for the next decade: early childhood education. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136761472/638501468/1641829122?refcode=ea.ad83af4f-cc91-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ms=ea.ad83af4f-cc91-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ5NTciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWQ4M2FmNGYtY2M5MS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZqelUU9yTjNvXj-Vb2e9RyDp0sBbcPfQV3aZnuOC6KM=) **At Let’s Grow Kids, I led a movement of over 40,000 parents, child care providers, and small business owners to pass the most significant child care law in the country.** We organized, we rallied, we fought, we came together across party lines, and _we won_ — even defeating Gov. Scott’s veto. One of the things I love about Vermont is that this is still a place where neighbors will set aside their differences, come to the table, and work together to make this state better. That’s what we did with child care at Let’s Grow Kids. **Our next governor needs to be able to create problem-solving coalitions on housing, health care, affordability, and more.** Peter, recent polling has shown that **_fewer than half_** of Vermonters think Gov. Scott is the right person for that job — and it’s shown that I am the **_most competitive Democrat_** running against him. **[Only five days remain for us to make that case to the remaining undecided voters in this Democratic primary. Peter, I try not to do so too often, but with less than a week until this primary is decided, = Before I say more, will you give me a few minutes of your time to reintroduce myself? I’m Aly Richards, proudly running to be your next Democratic governor of Vermont. = I grew up on a dirt road in Newbury. My parents believed that Vermont was the best place to raise a family. And they were right. I spent my summers fishing in my neighbors' pond, making strawberry jam, and square dancing at the town hall. I went to Oxbow High School, where my dad taught history. = After college, I wanted to do something — everything I could — to make a difference, and I quickly realized that change starts at home. After talking with Vermonters from all walks of life about the many issues we have to tackle, I concentrated on one project that became my focus for the next decade: early childhood education. = At Let’s Grow Kids, I led a movement of over 40,000 parents, child care providers, and small business owners to pass the most significant child care law in the country. We organized, we rallied, we fought, we came together across party lines, and we won — even defeating Gov. Scott’s veto. One of the things I love about Vermont is that this is still a place where neighbors will set aside their differences, come to the table, and work together to make this state better. That’s what we did with child care at Let’s Grow Kids. Our next governor needs to be able to create problem-solving coalitions on housing, health care, affordability, and more. Peter, recent polling has shown that fewer than half of Vermonters think Gov. Scott is the right person for that job — and it’s shown that I am the most competitive Democrat running against him. = | = Gratefully, Aly Richards = | | Aly is running for governor because she knows Vermonters are hungry for change — not more of the same. | A month ago, we did something the political establishment swore was impossible: we beat a 30-year incumbent right here in Colorado's 1st, powered by working people who refused to wait for permission.
I told you that primary night wasn't the finish line; it was the starting line. So last month, instead of taking a victory lap, I got on planes.
I traveled to Michigan to knock doors and rally in Detroit with my fellow DSA member Donavan McKinney and our friend Chris Rabb, proudly endorsed William Lawrence, a climate organizer fighting to flip one of the most competitive House seats in the country, and I rallied alongside Abdul El-Sayed as his history-making Senate campaign stood up to more than $30 MILLION in AIPAC spending.
---
| [](https://cefuo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001R0NrSQSsH3PU3xZoxpjjNXN33DIM6OSJ-uXeT5evv6-SFywqA7Nzu-LcXtUe3sRNWWY7cU9dgUtLTK7ksNWHufxoyG43R3VCnVSgMhqxvhwhQnH07hs2gUCiDRWrkIQqYPlAPgcWIuJOFTAXxBQR4yikmPnll9GYLV98vKcM4IBOxKpIJvFmJdlQeCtu5_m2zdLSJwVjsMMmikDIMKlXOPTsZSVY5exlnvhRwZTorEISYCgsp0vufA==&c=X_mI2mEQs_iF-H_V9hXDRiFeKCA0-HD4G218DoqDpAklFVZIAK5K3Q==&ch=gR-SPgMJxZFk9q747HtCdTYo0kBU0Od-8KWsnKUQUv5Vv7pR0MXnBA==)
